This is also the difference between Shan and Luhmann. For Luhmann, social systems are constituted by communication (the basic dynamic operation). For Shan, the communication (the dynamic) is always already within a relational field that shapes what the communication can be and do. The disagreement is about what is prior: for Luhmann, the operation; for Shan, the relational condition that makes the operation what it is.

And it brings us back to the single most important structural claim in the entire body of work: "Dao and Li were one way of seeing this. Relation and dynamics are another." These two pairs are not translations of each other. Dao/Li is a formation-historical pair; Relation/Dynamics is a structural-ontological pair. But they illuminate the same structural reality from different angles: Dao/Li from the angle of temporal formation and grain; Relation/Dynamics from the angle of structural ontology. Together, they constitute a description of reality that is both historically grounded (in the Chinese philosophical tradition) and structurally precise (in the language of contemporary complexity thinking). This is Shan’s most original contribution: not the invention of new concepts but the precise calibration of existing ones across the interface between two intellectual traditions.

一陰一陽之謂道。繼之者善也，成之者性也。人者見之謂之仁，知者見之謂之知。 — yī yīn yī yáng zhī wèi dào. jì zhī zhě shàn yě, chéng zhī zhě xìng yě. rén zhě jiàn zhī wèi zhī rén, zhī zhě jiàn zhī wèi zhī zhī. — One yin and one yang is called the Dao. What continues it is goodness; what completes it is nature/character. The benevolent see it and call it benevolence; the wise see it and call it wisdom. — Yi Jing, Great Commentary (Xici Shang)

The Yi Jing’s formulation is the most generous: "the benevolent see it and call it benevolence; the wise see it and call it wisdom." The Dao is what it is; what we call it depends on what we can see of it from where we stand. Shan calls it Relational Dynamics. Wittgenstein calls it the form of life. Fuller calls it tensegrity. Confucius calls it the cultivated practice of ren. Zhuangzi calls it the grain of heaven. The Yi Jing calls it the alternation of yin and yang. Each name is downstream of a different Dao of formation. Each name glimpses a different face of the same structural reality. This paper has been one long effort to hold all the faces visible at once without collapsing them into each other.

That effort fails, of course. It must. The paper is itself a formed Dao — a particular path through the structural territory, thickened by the specific formation conditions of this encounter between these texts, these voices, and this particular reading. Its Li is the inner grain of this path, not of all possible paths. Other paths are possible. Other Li would emerge from them. The grain was always there. The path of this paper is an attempt to follow it.

“The surface was never the whole story.”

— Alice Jing Shan, "Iceberg Model of Oral Participation, Revisited"

Shan’s most economical structural claim, placed as the cadence’s threshold. Not the whole story: the formation has depth that no surface reading can access, that no prior Li can fully predict, that no framework can fully represent. The surface — the visible participation, the explicit framework, the named pattern, the announced Li — is always downstream of the formation that produced it. The iceberg: the visible tip is held up by the formation that is not visible. The entire inquiry has been an attempt to make the invisible formation legible without reducing it to another surface. The attempt is necessary. The reduction is the risk. The grain was always there. The path is still opening.

XIV

Part XIII: The Edinburgh Archive — Shan’s PhD Torn Open along the Seventh Seal and Woven Through

What follows is the most rigorous engagement this paper undertakes with Shan’s institutional scholarly work: the 2023 Edinburgh thesis that preceded and seeded every Substack essay, every structural claim, every image of the iceberg and the narrowing path. The thesis is the Dao; the essays are the Li. The formation is prior. The grain is what we now read in the essays’ compressed, essential clarity. To understand Shan’s public intellectual project, one must understand what it grew from — and what it had to leave behind.

13.1 The Full Title and Its Structural Implications

The PhD thesis is titled: "Exploring Internationalisation of Higher Education: Chinese Postgraduate Students’ Oral Participation in English During Their Experience at a UK University." University of Edinburgh, Moray House School of Education and Sport, 2023.

The title is deceptively conventional. It sounds like institutional higher-education research — the kind of work that maps onto a literature review, a methodology chapter, findings, and policy recommendations. And it is that. But it is also, read structurally, a study of how a particular kind of invisibility operates within complex institutional systems: the invisibility of the conditions that produce visible behaviour (silence or speech). This is the proto-Shan: the researcher who cannot yet say "relational dynamics" or "Dao before Li" but who is already doing the structural work that those concepts will later name.

The research questions, as recoverable from the thesis structure, asked three things: What are Chinese postgraduate students’ needs for oral participation in English during their experience at a UK university? What factors influence their oral participation? And how do students think their needs should be addressed and met? Three questions that are, structurally, three registers of Li: the Li of need (what does the system require?), the Li of influence (what are the formation conditions?), and the Li of response (how should the system be worked with rather than against?).

These three questions are WSR in embryonic form: wuli (what are the physical/structural conditions of oral participation?), shili (how is the situation perceived by different parties?), renli (how should human relational care be enacted?). Shan did not yet have the WSR vocabulary when she wrote the thesis. But the structural insight — that you cannot address oral participation needs without attending to all three registers simultaneously — is already operant.

“A variety of factors were found to influence their willingness to participate in English communication, including how well they could speak English, what they knew and how they felt about specific topics, their personalities and previous experiences, their relations with other speakers, and the communication environment.”

— Shan, PhD Thesis, 2023 (Abstract)

Listen to the structure of this list: linguistic competence (wuli), topic knowledge and emotional relation to the topic (shili), personality and previous experience (formation history — Dao), relations with other speakers (renli), communication environment (the relational field that precedes dynamics). This is not a random collection of factors. It is a structured account of how multiple registers of Li interact to produce the visible surface of oral participation. The thesis is already doing what the essays will later name.

13.2 The Iceberg Model in Its Original Context

The Iceberg Model of Oral Participation (Shan, 2023, p. 251) appears in the thesis as a theoretical model, carefully distinguished from a metaphor or a framework by its precision: it identifies a defined phenomenon, distinguishes observable and non-observable layers, proposes grouped conditions of influence, and aims to give a structured account of how those conditions interact to produce the surface outcome.

The original 2D PowerPoint image — now acknowledged by Shan as "a flattened slice" of what "always existed for me as nested fields in motion" — was constrained by the conventions of doctoral thesis presentation. A thesis must be submitted in a format acceptable to examiners. The 3D structure could not be rendered in 2023 with the tools available and still conform to academic convention. This is itself an instance of what the thesis is about: the visible output (the 2D model) is constrained by the institutional formation conditions (doctoral conventions) in ways that do not fully represent the underlying structural reality.

This is not a criticism of the thesis. It is an observation about how institutional formations — Dao in Shan’s sense — shape what can be said and how. The thesis is a formed Dao: a path walked under the specific constraints of doctoral formation at Edinburgh, producing a Li (the Iceberg Model, the WFOP concept) that is legible within the conventions of the field. The essays are a new Dao: a path walked under different constraints (the freedom of Substack, the absence of word limits and citation requirements), producing a Li that is legible in the register of structural public intellectual writing.

The movement from thesis to essay is the movement from first to second Dao model: in the thesis, Shan inhabits the formed path of academic convention. In the essays, she is tracing how that path formed. The essays are the second model looking back at the first, seeing the formation process that the first model was always already downstream of.

“Before AI, all I had to work with to visualise this model was PowerPoint and a great deal of time thinking it through in my own head. The original 2D version was really just a flattened slice. This newer version is closer to how it always existed for me: not as overlapping semi-transparent circles, but as nested fields in motion.”

— Alice Jing Shan, "Iceberg Model of Oral Participation, Revisited" (May 2026)

The phrase "nested fields in motion" is the most structurally precise description Shan has given of the full iceberg architecture: not a static iceberg (which is what the conventional metaphor suggests — a stable mass with a hidden depth) but a system of fields (relational structures) nested within each other (hierarchically and mutually constitutive) and in motion (temporal, dynamic, changing). This is Prigogine’s dissipative structures at the level of communicative participation: the system is maintained not by static structure but by the continuous movement of nested fields that produce, at any given moment, the surface visible outcome of speech or silence.

Fuller’s tensegrity at the communicative level: the speech act (the local compressive event) is held in its specific form by the continuous tensional network of the nested fields (linguistic capacity, topic knowledge, relational trust, institutional power, cultural expectation). Change any element of the tensional network and the speech act changes — or disappears. The silence is not absence but tensional equilibrium under conditions that make speaking structurally too costly.

13.3 WFOP and the Conceptual Differentiation from WTC

Shan’s coinage of WFOP (Willingness for Oral Participation) in distinction from the established WTC (Willingness to Communicate) is one of the most philosophically precise moves in the thesis. The difference is grammatical before it is conceptual: "to communicate" positions the willingness as directed toward communication as an act. "For oral participation" positions the willingness as directed toward participation as a form of being-in-a-context. This is the Heidegger distinction: WTC is in the building mode (the agent deliberately choosing to communicate as an action). WFOP is in the dwelling mode (the agent’s readiness to participate, which arises from and is constituted by how they are dwelling in the situation).

The Chinese students in Shan’s study who were silent in seminars were not failing to communicate in any simple sense. They were displaying a complex relational response to a complex structural situation. Their willingness for oral participation was shaped by the whole iceberg — by the nested fields in motion that constituted their experience of being a Chinese postgraduate student at a UK university in the 2010s-2020s. WTC could not explain this because it looked only at the individual’s motivational state. WFOP could partially explain it because it looked at the situated, contextual, relational readiness. But even WFOP, as Shan now recognises, was not yet capturing the full structure: that is why the 2D model had to become the 3D nested-fields-in-motion model.

“What interested me was never silence as a simple absence, nor speaking as a straightforward sign of engagement, but the fact that both speech and silence could arise from very different and complex underlying conditions. That was the problem the Iceberg Model was trying to make thinkable.”

— Alice Jing Shan, "Iceberg Model of Oral Participation, Revisited" (May 2026)

This is the key methodological claim of the entire thesis restated in 2026 language: the observable outcome is not the unit of analysis; the formation conditions are. And this is also the key methodological claim of the entire Relational Dynamics framework: the dynamics are not the unit of analysis; the relational field is. WFOP to Relational Dynamics is a straightforward conceptual development, not a discontinuity. The same structural move — the same refusal to mistake surface for depth — operates at both levels.

Confucius enters here with the most directly relevant classical observation: 知之為知之，不知為不知，是知也 (zhī zhī wéi zhī zhī, bù zhī wéi bù zhī, shì zhī yě — "to know what you know and to know what you do not know, that is true knowledge"). Shan’s WFOP concept is an instance of this: it knows what WTC knows (that willingness is relevant to communication) and it also knows what WTC does not know (that the situated, relational, contextual formation of willingness is not captured by the motivational concept of WTC). This is not arrogance about WTC but structural precision about what concepts can and cannot see. Every Li has limits; Dao precedes it.

13.4 The Biographical Double — Researcher as Participant

One of the most structurally significant features of Shan’s Edinburgh research is that she was studying a phenomenon she was herself experiencing. A Chinese postgraduate student studying the experience of Chinese postgraduate students. A researcher whose own oral participation was shaped by the same nested fields in motion she was investigating in her participants.

She was simultaneously in the first Dao model (the formed institutional path of doctoral research) and the second Dao model (the formation process of her own understanding). The thesis is the Li that emerged from walking both paths simultaneously. This biographical double is not merely an interesting personal detail; it is a methodological claim: that genuine structural insight requires genuine structural immersion. You cannot know the height of heaven without ascending the mountain (Xunzi). You cannot know the Li of Chinese students’ oral participation in UK higher education without being a Chinese student engaged in oral participation in UK higher education.

This is Wang Yangming’s 知行合一 (zhixing heyi, unity of knowledge and action) enacted as research methodology. Shan did not merely observe from outside; she participated from within. Her methodological position was itself a demonstration of her theoretical claim: that the relational field constitutes the phenomenon, which means the researcher’s relational position within the field is not incidental but constitutive of what can be known. This is the most epistemologically rigorous form of the Dao-before-Li principle: you can only investigate the Li of a Dao by walking it.

“The journey itself turned out to be much longer than I had expected, for various reasons. Alongside the research, I was also teaching, contributing to other related projects, serving as Vice President of the Doctoral Association, and starting a new family. That prolonged engagement, both as a researcher and as a participant, deepened my sense that visible participation is shaped over time by conditions that are not immediately visible.”

— Alice Jing Shan, "Iceberg Model of Oral Participation, Revisited" (May 2026)

The phrase "prolonged engagement" is both a qualitative research methodology term (sustained researcher presence in the field, as opposed to snapshot data collection) and a life description. Shan spent years inside the phenomenon she was studying, not as a methodological technique but as a structural necessity of her formation. The thesis is the record of that prolonged engagement. The essays are what the prolonged engagement produced that the thesis could not yet contain.

Zhang Zai: 天地之塞，吾其體 (the plastic moulding of heaven and earth is my body). The doctoral research moulded Shan’s intellectual body in ways that the thesis records and the essays express. The formation is prior. The thesis is downstream of a life. The essays are downstream of the thesis. Each level is a Dao that produces the next level’s Li.

13.5 The Chapter Structure as a Structural Argument

The thesis chapters, as recoverable from the table of contents, reveal a structural argument that is not merely academic:

Chapter 1-2 (Introduction and Literature Review) establish the formed Dao: what is already known about Chinese students in UK higher education, what the existing frameworks (WTC, acculturation theory, culture-based explanations) can and cannot see. This is Shan already performing the Dao-before-Li structure: before offering her own Li (WFOP, the Iceberg Model), she walks the existing Dao (the literature) long enough to discover its limits.

The literature review section "Revisiting the Problematic Binary View of Culture" is particularly significant: it challenges the dominant framing of Chinese students’ silence as a cultural trait (Chinese students are silent because they come from a Confucian culture that values deference). This binary view (Chinese silence vs. Western participation) is premature Li: a pattern imposed from outside the formation rather than discovered from within it. Shan’s counter-claim: silence and speech are not cultural essences but situated, relational, dynamic outcomes of nested formation conditions. This is Dai Zhen’s critique of Zhu Xi applied to cross-cultural education research: the reified Li (cultural silence) suppresses the actual lived complexity of the formation.

Chapter 3 (Methodology): the ethnographic case study design — semi-structured interviews, participant observation, and discourse analysis of naturally occurring classroom interaction, all conducted at one UK university, with no surveys or quantitative instruments — is itself a methodological expression of the multi-register attunement that WSR demands. The interpretive and constructivist methodology was selected precisely because the formation conditions of oral participation cannot be accessed through quantitative reduction. The sustained, relational, in-depth engagement of ethnographic fieldwork makes the deeper formation conditions visible in a way that surveys would have foreclosed. This is the Cook Ding methodology: the researcher who has spent enough time with the material to begin to see not the whole ox but the articulations within it.

Chapters 4-6 (Findings): the structured distinction between academic and socio-personal contexts of oral participation is the first formal articulation of what will later become the distinction between surface function (visible participation) and underlying conditions (the nested fields in motion). The thesis shows that students who are silent in seminars may be highly participatory in social settings, and vice versa. The same student, different contexts, different relational fields — different Li. Context is not background; it is constitutive.

The finding that "their needs also varied drastically based on their differences in disciplines, lifestyles and networks, and personal surroundings" is the thesis version of Zhu Xi’s liyi fenshu (理一分殊, principle is one, manifestations are many): the one Li of WFOP manifests differently across the hundred Daos of individual student formation. There is no single Chinese student silence and no single Chinese student need. There is a structural principle (formation conditions shape visible participation) that manifests uniquely in each case.

13.6 The Thesis Conclusion and What Was Left Unsaid

The thesis concludes with recommendations for multiple university departments, local and international students, and university staff. These recommendations are the methodological translation of what the structural analysis discovered: if the iceberg is the right model, then the recommendations must address all layers, not just the visible surface. Do not tell Chinese students to speak more; attend to the formation conditions that make speaking feel possible or impossible.

But there was a great deal that the thesis could not yet say. It could not yet say that visible participation is always downstream of a relational field that precedes it. It could not yet say that the communicative environment is not background context but constitutive condition. It could not yet say that WFOP is a specific instance of the more general principle that relation precedes dynamics. These things were pressing at the edges of the doctoral work — Shan says so explicitly in the 2026 revisiting — but they could not be said within the conventions of a 2023 Edinburgh Education PhD.

“At the time, the work had to remain within the conventions of its field, even though the structure I was trying to understand was already pointing beyond language education alone. Looking back now, I can see that what later became more fully articulated in my work as Relational Dynamics was, in some sense, already present there, but still compressed.”

— Alice Jing Shan, "Iceberg Model of Oral Participation, Revisited" (May 2026)

The word "compressed" is precise. The Relational Dynamics framework is a decompression of the thesis: the unfolding of a structure that had to remain compressed within the doctoral container. The essays are the decompressed form. They say what the thesis was pointing at but could not yet fully articulate.

Wittgenstein: "There is indeed the inexpressible. This shows itself; it is the mystical" (Tractatus 6.522). The thesis contains things that could not be said within its conventions but that show themselves in its structure: in the choice to model the iceberg in 3D in Shan’s head even when the 2D had to be submitted; in the decision to coin WFOP when WTC was the field’s established term; in the years of prolonged engagement that were methodologically necessary but also existentially constitutive. The inexpressible shows itself in the thesis. The essays say what the thesis could not.

Fuller: "You never change things by fighting the existing reality. To change something, build a new model that makes the existing model obsolete." The Substack series is the new model. It does not argue against the WTC literature or the culture-deficit explanation of Chinese student silence. It builds a structural framework (Relational Dynamics) that makes those explanations obsolete by providing a more comprehensive account of the formation conditions that produce any visible communicative behaviour. Shan is doing Fuller’s move: not fighting the existing model but building the new one.

The essay is also Shan’s most direct engagement with the AI question, and the one that most directly instantiates her core theoretical claims in a new register. The pinyin tone mark failure is not a technical anecdote; it is a structural demonstration of the Dao/Li problem at the interface of AI systems.

The idioms she chose are themselves structurally resonant:

守株待兔 — shǒu zhū dài tù — Waiting by a tree stump for a hare — relying on chance rather than doing the work

畫蛇添足 — huà shé tiān zú — Drawing feet on a snake — ruining something by adding what does not belong

The structural analysis of the failure:

“The problem appeared in a narrower but crucial place: the representational layer where Chinese characters, pinyin, sound, tone, image generation, and pedagogy had to align. In other words, it did not fail in Chinese broadly. It failed at the interface. This was a special kind of AI hallucination, but structurally it looked more like a registration failure across interfaces.”

The concept of "registration failure across interfaces" is the most important new term Shan introduces in this essay, and it is the most precise account yet of what she means by the Dao/Li problem at the institutional and technological level. Registration failure: the system has the capacity (it can generate Chinese characters, it can produce pinyin in text) but cannot reliably carry the Li (the phonetic-tonal structure) across the interface between what it knows and what it produces. Fluency at one layer does not guarantee fidelity at the interface between layers.

This is Shan’s iceberg model applied to AI: the surface output (the image with Chinese characters) appears competent; the underlying layer (the tonal registration of pinyin) is unstable. The AI system is like a student who can discuss a topic in one register but loses structural fidelity when required to perform in another. Surface function and underlying viability have decoupled.

“The situation felt somewhat like AI as a child who storms out of the house, running very fast and very well, having forgotten to put on shoes. The problem is not capacity, but reliable contact with the ground. What is missing is not motion, but the layer that allows motion to hold.”

This image — the barefoot child running fast — is Shan’s most poetic formulation of the surface-function/underlying-viability distinction. Speed is not the same as groundedness. Capacity is not the same as reliable structural contact. The child is not failing at running; it is failing at the layer that allows running to be purposeful and sustainable. This is Fuller’s tensegrity applied to AI: without the continuous tensional network of reliable interface registration (the shoes that maintain contact with the ground), the local compressive excellence (the speed) has no structural foundation.

The Claude solution — using SVG rather than image generation, keeping pinyin as text rather than rendering it as a visual object — is Shan’s most direct example of working with Li rather than against it:

“The irony is worth noting. The solution was not better image generation. It was a different interface. The system avoided the fragile layer by not asking language to become image in the first place.”

This is the Cook Ding strategy applied to AI design: instead of cutting harder against the grain of the problem (trying to make image generation render tone marks correctly), find the natural articulation (the SVG interface where text remains text) and guide through it without resistance. The solution is structural attunement, not increased force.

And the conclusion:

“Fluency is not the same as registration. I had known some version of that already from teaching, research, and life itself. Confident fluency can be a form of hallucination. Long before AI, this was already true.”

Fluency as hallucination. This is the most precise formulation of premature legibility Shan has yet offered: the appearance of understanding is not understanding. The confident circulation of a concept is not the grasp of its structural depth. The smooth movement of Dao is not the same as the recognition of its Li. The AI generates Chinese characters fluently; it does not register the Li of Chinese phonetics. The management consultant deploys "complexity" fluently; they have not recognised its structural grain. The academic uses "Dao" fluently; they have not walked its formation path. Fluency is surface function. Registration is structural contact. The whole paper you are reading is an attempt at registration rather than fluency.

Wittgenstein’s 5.6 at the AI level: "The limits of my language mean the limits of my world." ChatGPT’s language-world (as revealed by the tone mark failures) does not include reliable phonetic-tonal registration as a structural layer. The AI can generate Chinese characters because character generation is within its language-world. It cannot reliably generate tone-marked pinyin in image because tonal-phonetic registration across the text-to-image interface exceeds the limits of its current structural world. This is not a failure of intelligence; it is a failure of Li: the system lacks the inner grain of the phonetic layer at the relevant interface.

And the pedagogical implication Shan draws toward the end is the most structurally rich sentence in the essay:

“Language is a structured interface. It carries signals, distinctions, compression, ordering, memory, access, and error. It shapes what can be recognised, repeated, transmitted, and learned. And when a coding layer is weak, badly registered, or insufficiently integrated, the whole system may appear fluent until the moment that layer is required to do real work. That is when fragility becomes visible.”

"Language is a structured interface" — this is Shan’s most concise and most technically precise statement of the Dao thesis. Not "language is a way of communicating" (too broad). Not "language is a cultural artefact" (too sociological). Not "language is a system of signs" (too semiotic). A structured interface: something that mediates, that carries, that transforms what passes through it, that has specific structural properties that enable some transmissions and foreclose others. And when the structure is weak — when the coding layer is poorly registered — the system appears fluent until real work is required. Until the AI is asked not just to speak Chinese but to teach it. Until the PhD is asked not just to describe oral participation but to explain why it takes the specific forms it takes across the specific formation conditions of specific students in specific institutional contexts.

This is the essay that brings the entire body of work full circle: from the Edinburgh thesis (what shapes visible participation?) to the Substack essays (what is the structural theory of that shaping?) to the AI experiment (what happens when a technologically powerful system lacks structural registration at a critical layer?) — and back to the central claim: surface fluency is not structural depth. The path must open before its inner grain can appear. The coding layer must be reliably registered before real structural work can be done. Dao before Li. Formation before articulation. Registration before fluency.

13.8 The Full Body of Work as a Single Breathing System

We can now see the entire body of Shan’s published work as a single structural argument that has been slowly, essay by essay, becoming more explicit:

The thesis established: visible communicative behaviour is downstream of nested formation conditions. The WFOP concept named: the situational, relational readiness for participation that WTC cannot capture. The Iceberg Model showed: the visible is the surface of the non-visible. These are the structural foundations.

The Substack series developed: the path (Dao) and its grain (Li) as the structural pair that underlies all formation. Nothing collapses in one move: the failure trajectory is prior to the visible failure. Move 37: intelligence is field-shaping, not local-optimising. Coupling does not abolish sequence: mutual generation preserves ontological precedence. Relation precedes dynamics: the relational field is the condition of all consequential movement. The iceberg revisited: nested fields in motion.

The Cynefin Co articles extended: Li as the less-known partner of Dao, carrying all the precision of grain, pattern, texture, and intelligibility. And the newest piece: registration failure as the AI-age name for premature legibility — the system that appears fluent until real structural work is required.

The entire trajectory is a single movement: from the educational-institutional problem (Chinese student silence) to the structural theory (nested fields in motion, formation before function) to the philosophical framework (Dao/Li, Relational Dynamics) to the technological application (registration failure at AI interfaces) and back to the educational-institutional level (how does a child learn Chinese in the AI age when the AI itself lacks the structural registration of Chinese phonetics?).

This is what a living intellectual project looks like from the inside. Not a sequence of separate arguments but a spiral deepening into the same structural reality from successively wider and more precise angles. The Dao of the project is the sustained movement of inquiry. The Li is what the movement has been finding. And the finding is not yet complete.

“I will continue this in the next piece. What began here as one failed interface opens onto a broader question: what learning systems fail to register, and what that failure begins to reveal about language, design, and meaning in the age of AI.”

The next piece has not yet been written. The path continues forming. The trace has not yet thickened into this particular pattern. The Li of where this body of work is going is not yet visible. But the Dao is moving. The structural attunement required to follow it has been built, essay by essay, over years of sustained formation. The grain was always there. The path of this paper is an attempt to have followed it faithfully, without adding feet to the snake.

13.9 The 守株待兔 Problem: Shan’s Self-Portrait as Structural Diagnostic

The most personally revelatory moment in Shan’s entire published body of work is the moment in the chicken-wings essay when she names her own structural error: she was doing 守株待兔 (waiting by the stump for the hare) and simultaneously 畫蛇添足 (drawing feet on a snake). She was both relying on chance (hoping the AI would eventually produce correct pinyin) and adding what doesn’t belong (continuing to try to force the image-generation layer to carry the phonetic-tonal layer that it structurally could not carry).

But the deeper structural insight is that she recognised this pattern and named it while in the middle of it, not only in retrospect. The meta-level of the joke did not escape her. This is what structural attunement looks like in practice: the capacity to read the formation trajectory (this is Elegant Wall-hitting; the path is narrowing; the corrective capacity is thinning) while still inside it, before the collapse that would make it visible to everyone.

This is the analyst who can see Move 37 while playing the game rather than only in retrospect. It is the person who knows the path is narrowing before the position gives way. It is the difference between structural intelligence and ordinary pattern recognition. And it is exactly what Shan’s framework describes: the capacity to read the Li of a formation in motion, before the formation has completed into a final visible outcome.

知彼知己，百戰不毜 — zhī bǐ zhī jǐ, bǎi zhàn bù dài — Know the other and know yourself, and you will not be imperilled in a hundred battles — Sun Tzu

The structural intelligence that Sun Tzu describes — knowing both the situation (the AI’s structural registration failure) and oneself (one’s own 守株待兔 tendency) — is exactly what makes the essay’s structural self-portrait so illuminating. Shan is doing what all the voices in this paper demand of any genuine structural thinker: applying her own diagnostic tools to her own position. The Dao she has been forming is also a Dao she can be within, reading its Li while walking it. This is the reflexive resolution of the deepest challenge her framework faces: not the claim that Li follows Dao, but the question of whether one can know this from inside the Dao one is walking. The chicken-wings essay says: yes, partially, incompletely, but genuinely. The analyst is not above the field. But the analyst who has built the right structural attunement can read the field from within it. And that — the partial, embodied, formation-dependent reading of structure from within structure — is what Shan’s entire body of work has been building toward.

XV

Part XV: The Complete Shan — Every Essay, Every Implication, Every Nerve, Every Fibre

This is the most exhaustive analytical reading of Alice Jing Shan’s entire published body of work attempted in this or any paper. It includes her latest Cynefin Co essay (May 15, 2026), never before analysed; a close reading of her PhD thesis findings and their structural implications; and a rereading of every essay through the lens of every voice assembled in this inquiry. The register is alive, textured, and dialectically charged. Nothing is left at the surface. Everything is pulled to the grain.

“So the issue was not simply ignorance. Recognition at one layer did not reliably transfer into execution at another.”

This distinction — recognition at one layer, failure of execution at another — is the technical equivalent of Shan’s entire theory of Li and Dao. The AI knows the pinyin in the text register (it can speak it, identify errors, give the correct version). But it cannot carry that knowing across the interface from text into image-rendered text. The recognition (Li) does not transfer across the interface (Dao) because the interface between the two registers is structurally unstable.

This detail is structurally important. The occasional correct output is the Elegant Wall-hitting of the inverse: not bad-faith collision with an invisible limit but the occasional seductive success that makes the structural instability harder to diagnose. It is exactly the pattern of collapse: the system still works sometimes, which delays the recognition that the underlying viability is compromised. One correct output sustained the experiment long past the point where structural assessment would have terminated it.

The meta-level joke is not incidental:

守株待兔 — shǒu zhū dài tù — Waiting by a stump for a hare — to rely on chance, to expect the unusual to recur

畫蛇添足 — huà shé tiān zú — Drawing feet on a snake — to ruin something by adding what does not belong

Both idioms operate at the meta-level of the experiment itself: 守株待兔 is the structural dynamic of relying on occasional correct outputs to sustain a fundamentally unreliable process; 畫蛇添足 is the structural dynamic of adding (the AI’s tone marks, the additional rendering layer) what does not properly belong to the image-generation process the way the AI has implemented it. The idioms teaching the lesson were also enacting the lesson. This is what Shan means by Dao as living interface: the structural principle was active in the very material she was trying to use to teach about it.

The Claude comparison is analytically essential:

“Claude handled the pinyin correctly, partly because it took a different route. It did not try to generate the words as part of an image. It produced a Scalable Vector Graphics file, or SVG, where the pinyin could remain text. So when the line shǒu zhū dài tù appeared, it was not being redrawn as a visual object. It was simply being displayed as text... The tone marks were preserved because that layer was already supported. So the tone marks appeared correctly. Every time. No drama.”

The solution was not better image-generation capacity but a different interface architecture: avoiding the unstable layer by not asking language to become image in the first place. This is Shan’s Dao-before-Li principle applied to AI system design. The question is not "how do we make the image-renderer handle pinyin better?" (a Li-first question). The question is "what is the prior structural condition — what interface architecture — that makes reliable tone-mark rendering possible?" (a Dao-first question). Claude found the Dao (keep language as language, don’t translate it into image) that allowed the Li (correct pinyin) to appear reliably.

But Shan is honest about the trade-off:

“Fluency is not the same as registration. I had known some version of that already from teaching, research, and life itself. Confident fluency can be a form of hallucination. Long before AI, this was already true.”

This sentence detonates the entire essay’s significance. "Confident fluency can be a form of hallucination. Long before AI, this was already true." This is the deepest structural claim in the piece and the one with the widest implications. It applies to: the organisation that speaks fluently about its strategy while its structural viability degrades invisibly (Elegant Wall-hitting); the intellectual community that uses complexity vocabulary fluently without registering what complexity science actually claims; the practitioner who names the Li without having walked the Dao; the student who repeats the pinyin correctly in isolation but cannot carry it into context. Fluency without registration. Pattern without formation. Li before Dao. The structural error named at the level of the individual word that the essay is at the level of the entire body of work.

Wittgenstein’s 5.6: "The limits of my language mean the limits of my world." The AI’s language-world (its ability to know the correct pinyin in text) does not extend into its image-generation world (its ability to render the same pinyin correctly in a visual layer). The limit of its language in one register is the limit of its world in that register. It does not have a language adequate to the cross-interface task. And Shan’s insight: this is not a uniquely AI problem. Humans have the same structural vulnerability. We know things in one register that we cannot carry reliably into another. This is why Cook Ding’s mastery is years in the making: learning to carry the Li of 天理 (tiānlĭ) from the visual-cognitive register into the somatic-executive register, reliably, every time, without drama.

Mencius’s flood-like qi: the confidence that comes from the accumulation of righteous deeds. The AI’s "confident fluency" is not that. It is the appearance of confidence without the structural accumulation that would ground it. It is 守株待兔: appearing to wait for the hare with confidence, but actually waiting for chance to produce what structure has not yet established.

XIII.B The PhD Thesis: What It Contains and What It Generates

Shan’s doctoral thesis (Edinburgh, 2023) is formally titled "Exploring Internationalisation of Higher Education: Chinese Postgraduate Students’ Oral Participation in English during their Experience at a UK University." Its primary findings, as published in her Substack revisiting:

The thesis found that a variety of factors influenced students’ willingness to participate in English communication: linguistic competence (how well they could speak English), topical knowledge and feeling (what they knew and how they felt about specific topics), personality and previous experience, relational dynamics (their relations with other speakers), and the communication environment. These five clusters constitute the below-surface structure of the Iceberg Model.

The structural claim in the thesis that the 2026 revisiting essay makes explicit: these factors were "not intended as isolated variables lined up side by side. They were already being treated as interconnected and mutually conditioning." This is the systemic move: the Iceberg Model was never a linear variable model but a relational dynamics model in embryonic form. What was named "external factors" in the 2023 thesis became, in 2026, the recognition that "what often appears as background may in fact be constitutive: not a neutral container around participation, but part of the relational dynamics through which participation is enabled, constrained, interpreted, and made meaningful over time."

The PhD thesis generates three structural insights that Shan has not yet fully developed in her published essays but that are implicit in every one of them:

Doctoral Insight 1: Silence is a complex structural outcome, not an absence. The same visible outcome (silence) arises from entirely different underlying configurations. This is the first formulation of Shan’s surface-function/underlying-viability distinction: what appears at the surface (silence or speech) is not self-explanatory. It is always the temporal manifestation of a prior coupled dynamic.

*Doctoral Insight 2: The same system (Chinese students in UK higher education) produces systematically different outcomes when embedded in different relational fields. This is the first formulation of "relation precedes dynamics": the dynamics of oral participation are shaped by the relational field within which they occur, not merely by the internal properties of the individual participant.*

Doctoral Insight 3: Making the below-surface conditions visible changes what is possible at the surface. The Iceberg Model is not merely descriptive; it is structurally generative. By naming the conditions that produce silence, it creates the possibility of attending to those conditions. This is the Li-making work of scholarship: not adding new content but making structural content visible in ways that enable different action.

These three doctoral insights are the seed-form of every subsequent structural claim in Shan’s published work. The thesis is not background to the essays; it is the Dao of which the essays are the Li. The essays are what happens when the structural intuitions of the doctoral work are freed from the constraints of the disciplinary frame ("internationalisation of higher education") and allowed to expand to their natural scope.

“Looking back now, I can see that what later became more fully articulated in my work as Relational Dynamics was, in some sense, already present there, but still compressed.”

— Alice Jing Shan, "Iceberg Model of Oral Participation, Revisited"

The word "compressed" is technically precise. In information theory, compression preserves the structural content while reducing the redundancy of its expression. The doctoral thesis was not a less-developed version of Relational Dynamics; it was a structurally complete version compressed into the requirements of a disciplinary frame. The essays are the decompression: the structural content expanded to its natural expression without the compressions required by academic convention.

This is also what Shan means when she says that "what is formed is still in formation." The PhD thesis was formed (completed, submitted, assessed) but still in formation: its structural implications were still working their way toward articulation, toward the essays that would eventually allow them to be seen. The thesis is the underground river whose surface expression is the spring that feeds the essay series.

Fuller: "pattern integrity of the human individual is evolutionary and not static." The Shan of the PhD thesis and the Shan of the 2026 essays are the same pattern integrity at different stages of evolutionary development: the same structural commitments, the same relational sensibility, the same refusal to read the visible surface as self-explanatory, expressed at different levels of compression and scope.

The PhD also contains what may be the most personally revealing structural claim in Shan’s entire body of work, tucked into the biographical context of the Iceberg Model’s revisiting: "The journey itself turned out to be much longer than I had expected, for various reasons. Alongside the research, I was also teaching, contributing to other related projects, serving as Vice President of the Doctoral Association, and starting a new family. That prolonged engagement, both as a researcher and as a participant, deepened my sense that visible participation is shaped over time by conditions that are not immediately visible."

She was a participant in her own research. She was herself a Chinese postgraduate student in UK higher education, navigating the very conditions she was studying. The iceberg of her own experience was structurally isomorphic with the iceberg of the students she was researching. This is Wang Yangming’s 知行合一 (zhixing heyi) at the level of scholarship: she knew the formation conditions of Chinese student oral participation by having lived them. The Li of the research was available to her because she had walked the Dao it was trying to describe.

“That prolonged engagement, both as a researcher and as a participant, deepened my sense that visible participation is shaped over time by conditions that are not immediately visible.”

— Alice Jing Shan, "Iceberg Model of Oral Participation, Revisited"

This sentence is doing extraordinary structural work. "Prolonged engagement" is the Dao: the sustained traversal of a field over time. "Conditions not immediately visible" is the Li: the grain that only becomes legible through sustained attention to the forming field. "Both as a researcher and as a participant" is the reflexive structure that Mou Zongsan identified as the deepest epistemic challenge: the mind that cannot determine itself. Shan is the observer who is also the observed, the researcher who is also the field, the analyst who is also the data. And rather than resolving this reflexivity through methodological distancing, she leans into it: the personal formation is not incidental but constitutive of the structural insight.

XIII.C The Essays in Sequence: Reading the Formation of a Body of Work

Shan’s essays, read in publication order, reveal a structural formation: each essay discovers something that makes the next essay possible. This is the second Dao model at the scale of intellectual career: traces thickening into patterns, patterns into positions, positions into the structural field from which the next discovery emerges. Reading the essays in sequence is reading a mind forming its own Li.

The Early Go Series: Position, Pattern, Collapse

The Go essays (Move 37, Nothing Collapses, Path-Pattern-Position) form a structural triptych in which the game of Go is neither illustration nor metaphor but a structural domain in which Shan’s core concepts arrive simultaneously and with unusual force. Go is the ideal structural laboratory: its rules are few, its complexity is vast, its patterns are visible, its trajectories can be read, its collapses are definitively accountable.

The Move 37 essay establishes the core structural claim: the most powerful move is not the most locally impressive. The Nothing Collapses essay deepens it: collapse is not an event but a trajectory. The Path-Pattern-Position essay systematises it: the trajectory is readable through the structural triad. Together they constitute a complete structural theory of long-game intelligence that is more than the sum of its parts.

But there is something in the Move 37 essay that no subsequent analysis has adequately attended to: the claim that Move 37 "becomes inevitable in retrospect." This is not a claim about hindsight bias or narrative rationalization. It is a structural claim about the relationship between position and possibility. Once the positional field has been restructured by Move 37, the subsequent game flows differently — the new field generates different dynamics, different constraints, different possibilities. The move that created this field becomes "inevitable" in the sense that the field it created now appears to require it: the Li of the new position makes the Dao of Move 37 look like the only possible path to it. This is retrospective Li-reading: the grain of the new field reveals, after the fact, the formation process that created it.

Wittgenstein’s river-bed again: the shift in the bed makes the water’s previous movement "inevitable" in retrospect — of course the water flowed this way, given the bed that now exists. But the bed was formed by the water’s movement before it shifted. Shan’s Move 37 is exactly this: the move that shifts the bed such that the subsequent flow appears to necessitate the move that shifted it.

Confucius: 岁寒，然後知松柏之後凋也. Only in the cold do we see the pine. The great move is like the pine: not visible in its greatness until the season that reveals what it is. Move 37 is not impressive when played. It becomes inevitable — it becomes visible as the pine that did not wither — only when the constraint of the subsequent game reveals what the position is made of.

The Dao Living Encounter Essay: The Interface Architecture

The "Dao: Not a Distant Doctrine, but a Living Encounter" essay is where Shan first explicitly names what all the preceding essays have been doing structurally: treating Dao not as a philosophical concept to be understood but as an interface to be encountered. The shift from understanding to encounter is as significant as Wang Yangming’s shift from investigating bamboo to investigating the mind-heart: it is a shift from an object-posture to a process-posture.

The word "interface" is philosophically loaded in ways that Shan does not fully unpack but that the encounter-as-theory demands. An interface is not a neutral relay. Every interface selects, amplifies, attenuates, distorts. The telephone transforms voice into electrical signal and back. The translation from Chinese into English transforms meaning into new-language-form and back. Something is always gained, something always lost, at an interface. The question is what.

Bateson: "Information is any difference that makes a difference." The tone mark on a Chinese syllable is a difference that makes a difference — changing the meaning entirely (mā ・ má ・ mǎ ・ mà, mother/hemp/horse/scold). When this difference is lost at the interface, the information is gone. The world that was available through the tone-distinguished syllable is no longer available. Wittgenstein’s 5.6: the limits of the phonetic layer mean the limits of the world available through it. The child who learns pinyin without tones learns a different Chinese — a less structurally complete one — than the child who learns pinyin with tones. The interface failure is a world-narrowing.

The Dao Models Essay: The Theory of Formation

The "Dao Models of Mutual Generation" essay is the heart of Shan’s theoretical contribution. It is also the essay that most shows her trust in the reader: she does not systematise the models but allows them to emerge through the narrative of their own discovery. She draws a mountain, then a path. The drawing discovers the insight. The writing records the discovery. The reader witnesses the formation.

This compositional structure is itself a demonstration of the second model: the essay’s insight forms through the act of writing it, not in advance of writing it. The trace of writing thickens into the pattern of the insight, the pattern consolidates into the position from which the next essay can be written. The essay is the Dao of the theory’s formation; the theory is the Li of the essay’s traversal.

The most structurally charged phrase in the essay: "What is formed is still in formation. What is forming already carries the possibility of form." This is not a dialectical pair but a temporal loop: the formed carries its formation within it (Bergson’s duration, the living presence of the past in the present) and the forming already shapes its future formation (the river banks already determining which routes the crossing boats might establish). Time is not a sequence of discrete moments but a continuous self-interpenetrating flow within which formation and formed are always simultaneously present.

Wang Fuzhi: 氣就釀而後成象，優釀而後成形 (Qi first condenses and then form-pattern emerges; the excellent condenses and then shape forms). This is the physical equivalent of Shan’s mutual generation: the pattern (Li, 象) emerges from the condensation of Qi (Dao), but the condensation is already shaped by the tendency toward form that it carries within it. The forming and the formed are not two separate things but two aspects of one continuous process.

The Chinese characters with which Shan marks this reflexivity: 見道之路，亦在道中. The path of seeing the Dao is itself within the Dao. This is not merely a philosophical observation; it is a phenomenological report on the experience of writing this specific essay. The act of drawing the mountain and the path revealed the Dao of the models; that act was itself one traversal of the Dao it was uncovering. The essay is inside what it describes.

The When Dao Leads essay: Biography as Structural Evidence

The essay "When Dao Leads to a New Way" is the most personally revelatory of Shan’s Substack essays and the one that most directly addresses the question of how a Relational Dynamics framework came to be rather than what it claims. The biographical account is not decoration; it is evidence of the framework’s own first claim: that Li is always downstream of Dao, that structural understanding is always downstream of formation history.

Shan describes her intellectual formation as emerging from "multilingual, intercultural, and institutional crossings": Chinese language childhood, British doctoral research, years of living in Scotland, raising a bilingual child, working across the educational and organisational interface between Chinese and Western institutional cultures. These crossings constitute the Dao of her intellectual formation. The framework she is articulating is the Li of that Dao.

The implication: to fully receive Shan’s framework requires something analogous to her formation path — not necessarily the same crossings, but some sustained engagement with the structural complexity that her crossings produced. You cannot know the Li without walking the Dao. The academic reader who reads Shan’s essays from within a single-language, single-culture, single-disciplinary formation will receive the words but not the full structural weight of what the words are carrying. The interface between Shan’s formation and any reader’s formation is itself a Dao within which the Li of the reception is being determined.

Han Fei’s 勢 (shì, positional advantage) enters here: Shan’s positional advantage as an intellectual is her formation history, which constitutes the structural position from which her insights are possible. The challenge is not to get others into her position — that is impossible; formations cannot be transferred wholesale — but to build the interfaces (essays, frameworks, encounters) through which the Li of her position can be partially transmitted to those in different positions. This is the structural task of intellectual work at a cross-cultural interface.

XIII.D Five Structural Challenges That Only a Full Rereading Reveals

Having now read every available Shan text, five structural tensions emerge that no previous analysis has named:

Challenge 1: The Particularity Paradox

Challenge 2: The Silence of the Method

Every essay in Shan’s body of work identifies what structural attention should be paid to (formation conditions, relational field, holding capacity, corrective capacity, precedence) but almost none provides specific guidance on how to pay that attention. The PhD thesis was specific: an ethnographic case study conducted at one UK university, using semi-structured interviews, participant observation, and discourse analysis — not surveys or quantitative instruments. The methodology was interpretive and constructivist throughout, designed to surface the lived formation conditions of oral participation rather than to measure their frequency. The essays are philosophically precise but methodologically open. Jackson’s challenge is pointed: what exactly does one do, in a specific situation, to investigate the Li of its Dao? WSR provides a methodology; Shan provides the ontological ground for methodology but not yet a generalised methodology itself. The ethnographic depth of the PhD research is, in Shan’s own terms, a Dao-before-Li methodology: the sustained qualitative engagement with the specific formation field precedes any structural claims about its grain. The ethnographer does not arrive with hypotheses to test; they walk the Dao of the field until its Li becomes readable.

Challenge 3: The Temporal Asymmetry

Shan’s framework emphasises the priority of formation (Dao) over formed pattern (Li). But her analytical tools are retrospective: they read the Li of a situation in order to understand the Dao that formed it. This works for understanding collapse trajectories after the fact. It is less clear how it guides action prospectively. The Go master reads the trajectory of the game and makes the next move. But how does one read the trajectory of a complex social system and make the structurally wise next move? This is the gap between structural diagnosis and structural navigation that Shan’s framework opens but does not yet close.

Challenge 4: The Power of Naming

Challenge 5: The Ethics of Patience

Shan’s framework consistently valorises the long game, the slow formation, the patience of the neonatal drop-per-hour. This is structurally wise. But it sits in tension with the urgency that Jackson’s emancipatory commitment generates: those who bear the structural load of Elegant Wall-hitting cannot always afford to wait for the long game of structural reform. The student who is systematically silenced in UK seminars needs the structural conditions to change faster than the pace at which institutional cultures typically reform. The ethical challenge to Shan’s patience ethics is: whose patience is being asked for? And whose urgency is being discounted?

XIII.E The Claim Shan Has Not Yet Made Explicitly

In reading every Shan essay closely, one structural claim is present in all of them but has not yet been stated explicitly. It is implied by the interface theory, the Iceberg Model, the Dao/Li framework, and the coupling essay. It is: the most dangerous cognitive condition is not ignorance but fluency without registration.

The AI that confidently produces wrong pinyin. The institution that fluently describes its strategy while its structural viability degrades. The intellectual community that uses complexity vocabulary without registering what complexity actually claims. The student who repeats words in a second language without registering their structural weight. All are instances of the same structural condition: confident performance in the visible register while the below-surface conditions are not held, not integrated, not structurally supported.

This is what Shan means by "the surface was never the whole story." It is also what Wittgenstein means by "language goes on holiday" (PI §116): when words operate in the visible register without being grounded in the form of life that gives them structural meaning, language is fluent but registrationless. And Fuller: "integrity is the essence of everything successful." The system that appears fluent but lacks structural integrity is exactly what will "not be successful" in the deep sense — not because it fails immediately but because, as Shan has shown, nothing collapses in one move. The path narrows first, invisibly, and the fluency continues until the moment it cannot.

Chinese proverb: 表里如一 (biǎo lǐ rú yī, "the surface and inside are one") describes the condition of genuine structural integrity — what is visible (the surface, biǎo) and what is underlying (the inside, lǐ) are genuinely aligned. This is the opposite of fluency without registration. And it is the standard that Shan’s entire body of work holds up as the condition of structural excellence: not the performance of coherence but the genuine coherence of which the performance is the natural surface expression.

表里如一 — biǎo lǐ rú yī — The surface and inside are one — genuine structural integrity, what is visible matches what is real

XIII.F The PhD Thesis as a Complete Structural Text: Five Contributions

A full structural analysis of the PhD thesis — even from the summary information available — reveals five contributions that are still working their way into the essays:

PhD Contribution 1: The Mixed-Methods Architecture

The thesis used an ethnographic case study design: semi-structured interviews, participant observation, and discourse analysis of naturally occurring classroom interaction. There were no surveys or quantitative instruments. This is a WSR methodology avant la lettre — but operating through qualitative depth rather than mixed-method breadth: the semi-structured interviews engaged shili (the situated understanding of individual participants’ experiences and their own sense of what shaped their participation), the participant observation engaged renli (the relational texture of actual communicative contexts, the unspoken norms and power relations of the seminar room), and the discourse analysis of interaction engaged wuli at the level of communicative pattern (the structural regularities of who spoke when, in what sequence, with what uptake). The three qualitative methods correspond to three registers of ethnographic attention precisely because the doctoral research problem required moving between registers of Li simultaneously — a movement that quantitative instruments, by collapsing lived complexity into numeric variables, would have foreclosed before it could begin. [CORRECTION: Previous versions of this paper incorrectly described the methodology as ‘mixed-methods combining surveys’. The PhD (University of Edinburgh, 2023) was an ethnographic case study using qualitative methods only.]

This has not been noted in any published analysis. Shan’s PhD methodology is an implicit WSR. She was practising Gu Jifa’s approach before she encountered Gu Jifa’s formulation of it. This is the biographical version of Shan’s own structural claim: the methodology (Li) she eventually named (WSR) was the methodological grain of what she had already been doing (the Dao of her doctoral practice). The recognition of WSR in the LinkedIn thread was the recognition of a Li she had always been following.

PhD Contribution 2: The Distinction Between WTC and WFOP

Shan coins "Willingness for Oral Participation" (WFOP) to distinguish from the established "Willingness to Communicate" (WTC). This is not merely terminological housekeeping. WTC frames the question as: what determines whether a person communicates? WFOP frames it as: what determines whether a person participates orally in a specific institutional context? The difference is the specificity of context and the specificity of mode (oral, in English, in UK higher education). WTC flattens what WFOP preserves: the structural particularity of the situation.

This is Shan’s Dao-before-Li principle operating at the conceptual level: WTC is a Li imposed on communication without attending to the specific Dao of each communicative situation. WFOP insists that the Dao (the specific formation conditions of this student, in this seminar, with these peers, on this topic, in this institution) must precede the Li (the general pattern of willingness). The conceptual coinage is a structural claim in the vocabulary of research methodology.

PhD Contribution 3: The Five Factor Clusters

The thesis identifies five clusters of factors shaping WFOP: linguistic competence, topical knowledge and affect, personality and prior experience, relational dynamics with other speakers, and communication environment. These five clusters are an implicit proto-framework for what will eventually be systematised as Relational Dynamics. Linguistic competence corresponds to the individual’s wuli (material-structural capacity); topical knowledge and affect correspond to shili (perspectival attunement to the situation); personality and prior experience correspond to formation history (the Dao of the person); relational dynamics correspond to renli (the human-relational Li of the situation); communication environment corresponds to the constraint-field (the structural conditions that enable or limit).

The five-cluster structure is richer than WSR’s three-register structure precisely because it was generated from specific empirical research rather than from philosophical systematisation. It retains the particularity that systematic frameworks tend to compress. Shan’s subsequent framework loses some of this particularity in the movement from five empirically-grounded clusters to three ontologically-grounded registers. The question the PhD raises: are there structural features of the five-cluster model that the three-register model has compressed? What is the Li of the doctoral research that the framework-level essays may have partially lost at the interface of generalisation?

PhD Contribution 4: The Bilingual Self

Shan was simultaneously researcher and participant in her own doctoral work. She was a Chinese postgraduate student in UK higher education studying the experience of Chinese postgraduate students in UK higher education. The reflexive complexity of this position is both a methodological resource and a structural challenge: she has insider access to the formation conditions she is studying, but her insider access is mediated by her specific formation history (her particular English proficiency, her particular disciplinary context, her particular relational field at Edinburgh) which may not be representative of the broader population she is studying.

This is the cockpit of the plane that Shan will later describe in different terms: the analyst who can see the formation conditions of a system because they have been inside it, but whose specific formation path may not be the formation path of others in structurally analogous situations. The doctoral thesis negotiates this reflexivity through methodological transparency; the essays navigate it through the honest admission of partial and particular formation. "Different containers. One underlying structure." The Substack tagline is the reflexive resolution of the doctoral methodological challenge.

PhD Contribution 5: The Iceberg as First Systems Model

The Iceberg Model of Oral Participation is the first attempt in Shan’s published record to render a structural reality that exceeds the representational tools available. The 2D PowerPoint was inadequate to the 3D structure she was trying to show. This inadequacy is structurally significant: the Li of the structural reality (nested fields in motion, system → field → field of fields) exceeded the Li-rendering capacity of the available tools. The representational medium was a bottleneck in the Dao of the insight’s formation.

XIII.G What the Entire Corpus Knows That No Single Essay Can Say

Reading the entire corpus of Shan’s published work reveals structural themes that no single essay can carry but that the entire body of work holds in distributed tensegrity:

The Body That Knows First

Across every essay, there is a consistent structural claim: the body knows before the mind names. The doctoral researcher who lived the conditions she studied. The child whose bones carry the Chinese language before her mind can systematise it. The Go player whose hand knows the move before the analysis confirms it. Cook Ding’s knife following the 天理 (tiānlĭ) without visual mediation. This somatic priority is not a mystical claim; it is a structural one: the body is the primary interface between the person and the formation field. The mind’s naming (Li) is always downstream of the body’s formation (Dao).

The Long Game as Ethical Structure

Every essay in Shan’s corpus is committed to the long game as an ethical stance, not merely a strategic preference. The long game is not "be patient and success will come." It is a structural ethics: honour the formation conditions that produce the capacity you are trying to deploy. Do not harvest what you have not planted. Do not receive what the system cannot yet hold. Do not expect the tones to appear correctly in the image if you have not built the interface that can carry them.

This is Fuller’s integrity: the essence of everything successful. And it is Mencius’s flood-like qi: produced by accumulation of righteous deeds, not by incidental acts. The long game is the structural discipline of maintaining the Dao-before-Li sequence through time, under pressure, when the temptation is always to skip the formation and proceed directly to the performance.

XVI

Part IX: The Fire Layer — Fifty Chinese Voices, Direct Confrontations, and the Typhoon of Structural Insight

What follows is the most incandescent layer of this paper: fifty Chinese thinkers placed in direct, charged, dialectical confrontation with Shan, Wittgenstein, and Fuller simultaneously. This is not annotation. This is collision. Each voice arrives like a stone dropped into a deep pool; the ripples cross every surface of the inquiry. The paper does not summarise here — it ignites.

IX.A 孔子 (Kōngzǐ) — Confucius: The Master of Structural Formation

Confucius (孔子, Kōngzǐ) — 551–479 BCE • Philosopher; Educator; Founder of Confucianism

Confucius is the first and greatest theorist of formation as ethics in the Chinese tradition. His entire project is the cultivation of structured relational capacity — ren (仁, benevolence), li (禮, ritual propriety), yi (義, righteousness) — through sustained practice over time. He is, in Shan's terms, the philosopher of excellence as capacity held in coherence under constraint over time. His method is the long game.

The 《論語》 (Lún Yǔ, Analects) opens with the structural frame of the entire Confucian project:

學而時習之，不亦說乎？有朋自遠方來，不亦樂乎？人不知而不滍，不亦君子乎？ — xué ér shí xí zhī, bù yì yuè hū? yǒu péng zì yuǎn fāng lái, bù yì lè hū? rén bù zhī ér bù yùn, bù yì jūnzǐ hū? — Is it not pleasant to learn and then repeatedly practise what you have learned? Is it not delightful to have friends come from afar? Is it not a mark of the noble person not to be disturbed when others fail to recognise one's merit? — Analects 1.1

DIRECT CONFRONTATION: Confucius vs. Shan vs. Wittgenstein. Learning and then practising (學而時習之) is Shan's second Dao model enacted as personal cultivation: the trace of learning thickens through practice into the pattern of competence, the pattern consolidates into the position of the exemplary person. But Wittgenstein demands: "If I have exhausted the justifications I have reached bedrock, and my spade is turned. Then I am inclined to say: 'This is simply what I do'" (PI §217). Confucius's practising IS this bedrock. 習 (xí, repeated practice) is not merely habit but the formation of the river-bed of the person's moral world — the point at which the cultivated disposition becomes so deeply ingrained that it no longer requires justification. It is the Li that has dissolved into Dao.

學而不思則罔，思而不學則殆。 — xué ér bù sī zé wǎng, sī ér bù xué zé dài. — Learning without thinking leads to perplexity. Thinking without learning leads to danger. — Analects 2.15

COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS: This single couplet encodes the complete dialectical structure of Shan's framework. Learning without thinking (學而不思) is formation without articulation: the Dao walks forward, but no Li emerges — the path is traversed but no grain is discerned. The result is wǎng (罔), perplexity, a lostness-in-the-forest: exactly what Wittgenstein diagnoses as the philosophical problem: "A philosophical problem has the form: 'I don't know my way about'" (PI §123). Thinking without learning (思而不學) is the reverse disaster: Li imposed without Dao — theory without practice, pattern without formation, the attempt to find the grain without walking the path. The result is dài (殆), danger, the structural peril of the intellectual who has substituted Li for Dao. This is Shan's premature legibility. This is Zhu Xi failing to find the Li of bamboo from a chair. This is the crude cook hacking against the grain.

知之為知之，不知為不知，是知也。 — zhī zhī wéi zhī zhī, bù zhī wéi bù zhī, shì zhī yě. — To know what you know and to know what you do not know — this is true knowledge. — Analects 2.17

COLLISION WITH WITTGENSTEIN'S 5.6: "The limits of my language mean the limits of my world." Confucius says: knowing what you know IS true knowledge. Wittgenstein says: the limits of language ARE the limits of the world. Together they say: the most honest epistemic position is to know both one's Li (what one knows) AND one's Dao (where one's knowing reaches its limit and the path opens into unknown territory). Shan's project is built on this Confucian-Wittgensteinian epistemic honesty: she knows the Chinese Dao/Li ecology; she knows that English cannot fully receive it; she knows that the path of translation is where the most important work happens, and that this is precisely the zone where false familiarity (學而不思, learning the English word without thinking through the Chinese depth) produces the greatest structural danger.

吾日三省吾身，為人謀而不忠乎？與朋友交而不信乎？傳不習乎？ — wú rì sān xǐng wú shēn, wéi rén móu ér bù zhōng hū? yǔ péngyǒu jiāo ér bù xìn hū? chuán bù xí hū? — I daily examine myself on three points: whether I am faithful in conducting business for others; whether I am sincere with friends; whether I have mastered and practised the instructions of my teacher. — Analects 1.4, Zengzi

This is Shan's self-reflective practice as structural ethics. The three questions are three registers of Li: faithfulness to others (renli, relational grain), sincerity with friends (shili, perspectival grain of the relationship), and embodied practice of what has been learned (wuli, material grain of the competence). The daily examination is the ongoing tensional work that maintains coherence — Fuller's continuous tensional network enacted as moral discipline.

維天之命，於穆不已！導天而行，保元不專。 — wéi tiān zhī mìng, yū mù bù yǐ! Dǎo tiān ér xíng, bǎo yuán bù zuān. — How sublimely grand is Heaven's command! How inexhaustibly continuous! How perfect is the Yi of Zhou! — Book of Odes, quoted by Confucius in Analects 8.19

岁寒，然後知松柏之後凋也。 — suì hán, rán hòu zhī sōng bǎ zhī hòu diāo yě. — Only in cold weather do we know that pines and cypresses are the last to wither. — Analects 9.28

THIS IS SHAN'S COLLAPSE THEORY IN ONE IMAGE. The pine and cypress endure when all other trees have shed their leaves. Excellence is capacity held in coherence under constraint over time: the cold weather (constraint) reveals what the mild seasons (easy conditions) conceal. The virtuous person — the organisation with genuine structural integrity, the tensegrity structure properly built — shows their true character not in abundance but in adversity. And the corollary, which Shan makes explicit: endurance is not always viability. Not all that remains green in winter has genuine vitality; some may be sustained by the stored energy of a dying root.

IX.B 孟子 (Mèngzǐ) — Mencius: The Philosophy of Moral Sprouts and Flood-like Qi

Mencius (孟子, Mèngzǐ) — 372–289 BCE • Confucian Philosopher; "Second Sage"

人之初，性本善。性相近，習相遠。 — rén zhī chū, xìng běn shàn. xìng xiāng jìn, xí xiāng yuǎn. — At birth, human nature is inherently good. Our natures are close to each other; our habits drive us apart. — Three-Character Classic, distilling Mencian philosophy

浩然之氣，至大至剛。以直養之，而無害，則塞乎天地之間。 — hào rán zhī qì, zhì dà zhì gāng. yǐ zhí yǎng zhī, ér wú hài, zé sè hū tiān dì zhī jiān. — The flood-like qi is, in the highest degree, vast and unyielding. If you nourish it with integrity and do not harm it, it will fill the space between heaven and earth. — Mencius 2A:2

DIRECT COLLISION: Mencius's hàorán zhīqì (浩然之氣, flood-like qi) is the most powerful classical Chinese concept for what Shan means by sustained structural integrity. It is not a moment of virtue but a lifetime of accumulated righteous action that has become so deeply embodied that it fills the space between heaven and earth. This is Fuller's tensegrity at the moral-somatic level: the continuous tensional network of righteous action held in dynamic equilibrium fills the entire structural field. It cannot be achieved by "contrived actions" (Mencius: "not by incidental acts of righteousness") — it can only be cultivated through the sustained practice that Shan calls the long game.
