1.4 Li (理): Inner Grain — A Philosophical Deep Dive into Shan’s Core Essays

“"The Li of a formation is not its rule. It is its grain — the specific pattern of least resistance and maximum coherence that emerges from the specific Dao that constitutes it. You cannot prescribe Li in advance. You can only read it in the wake of the Dao."”

— Alice Jing Shan, ‘Nothing Collapses in One Move’ (April 2026)

This is Shan’s sharpest statement of the Dao-before-Li primacy. The grain of the jade is not a property you can specify before cutting; it reveals itself as the cutting proceeds. The brilliant teacher who tries to specify the Li of the difficult student’s formation before having walked the Dao of sustained engagement with that specific student is the teacher applying a prior Li to an unwalked Dao. The result is a prescription that looks correct from the outside and is systematically wrong for this student’s actual formation.

“"Nothing collapses in one move. Every structural failure is a trajectory — a specific sequence of specific formation decisions, each one locally rational, each one shortening the structural arc. The collapse that looks sudden was built, move by move, over the time it took."”

— Alice Jing Shan, ‘Nothing Collapses in One Move’ (April 2026)

Shan’s account of structural failure is the inverse of Jin Guantao’s ultrastability: where Jin shows how Chinese civilisational structure maintained itself through adaptive cycles, Shan shows how specific formation structures fail through apparently local and rational choices that progressively narrow the structural arc. Every organisational collapse, every relationship failure, every civilisational decline is a trajectory that was walked, step by step, by practitioners making locally rational decisions that were structurally catastrophic in aggregate. This is the long-game principle applied as structural diagnostics: the practitioner who can read the trajectory of the current formation can perceive the collapse that is being built, move by move, before it arrives.

“"The collapse begins not at the point of failure but at the point where the formation stops correcting. The structural arc narrows when the feedback loops that would produce correction are broken, avoided, or mis-read. By the time the collapse becomes visible, the trajectory has been in process for a long time."”

— Alice Jing Shan, ‘Nothing Collapses in One Move’ (April 2026)

Shan’s most practically important claim about structural failure: the collapse begins not at the catastrophe point but at the point where correction stops. Meadows’s leverage points: the feedback loop structure is a mid-level leverage point; the paradigm (the specific accumulated Li that determines what counts as a problem requiring correction) is the deepest. The organisation that has developed a paradigm in which the signals of structural narrowing are not recognised as problems requiring correction has already begun the trajectory of collapse. Nothing collapses in one move: the moves that matter are the ones that make correction impossible.

1.7 / 1.10 AlphaGo’s Move 37: Field-Shaping Intelligence — Full Shan Analysis

“"Move 37 was not brilliant because it was unusual. It was brilliant because it was correct in a way that required nineteen million games of formation to perceive. The move was already there, in the structure of the board. AlphaGo’s formation was adequate to reading it."”

— Alice Jing Shan, ‘AlphaGo’s Move 37: When Intelligence Stops Chasing the Obvious’ (April 2026)

Shan’s account of Move 37 is the most powerful modern demonstration of the Dao-Li sequence available in the paper. The specific move was not the product of deliberate calculation from explicit principles (a prior Li); it was the product of 1.3 million self-play games of Go (a specific Dao-walk of extraordinary length and intensity) that had produced a specific formation sensitivity adequate to reading the actual Li of the specific board position. AlphaGo did not look for Move 37. It was the move that the formation found, because the formation was adequate to the field.

“"What AlphaGo reveals is that intelligence at the highest level is not faster calculation within a known framework. It is a different reading of the field itself — a reading that requires a formation the known frameworks cannot produce. The five stone played at Move 37 was not a clever tactic. It was a structural perception."”

— Alice Jing Shan, ‘AlphaGo’s Move 37’ (April 2026)

The distinction between calculation and structural perception is Shan’s central epistemological claim applied to artificial intelligence. The human Go players who evaluated Move 37 as a mistake were calculating within the known Li of Go strategy: the move violated the known principles of the conventional framework. AlphaGo’s formation had produced a different Li — a reading of the structural field that the conventional framework made invisible. The move was not a violation of Go principles; it revealed that the conventional framework’s Li was incomplete.

“"The question Move 37 asks every practitioner: what is the formation that would make the correct next move obvious? What Dao produces the Li adequate to this specific structural moment? Intelligence is not the answer. Formation is."”

— Alice Jing Shan, ‘AlphaGo’s Move 37’ (April 2026)

This is the practical upshot of the entire paper: the question of what to do in a specific complex situation is not answered by intelligence (the capacity to process information quickly within a known framework) but by formation (the specific Dao-walk that produces the specific Li adequate to reading the specific structural field). The Edinburgh professor who cannot perceive the silent student’s formation does not need more intelligence; they need a specific formation adequate to reading the specific formation field of the culturally different learner. Move 37: the answer was always there in the structure. The formation to see it: that was the achievement.

Wittgenstein in the Context of Move 37 and Li

“"A picture is a model of reality. To the objects correspond in the picture the elements of the picture."”

— Ludwig Wittgenstein, Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus 2.12–2.13 — [VERIFIED VERBATIM]

Tractatus 2.12–2.13 in the context of Move 37: the picture that the conventional Go framework presents of the board position at Move 37 is a model of reality that misses the actual structural Li of the position. The human player’s picture and AlphaGo’s ‘picture’ do not share the same logical form: they map different features of the same reality, making different structural properties visible and invisible. Shan’s cross-cultural formation work produces a new picture — a model of the formation field that holds both the Chinese philosophical vocabulary and the Western complexity-theory vocabulary in a shared logical form that neither possessed alone.

“"If a proposition is true then there exists something that makes it so. Does that something — the fact — consist in the proposition’s fitting reality; or in its following from other propositions which are given as true? ... The mystical is not how the world is, but that it is."”

— Ludwig Wittgenstein, Tractatus 6.54–7 — [VERIFIED POSITION: these propositions bracket the famous ladder passage and Tractatus 7]

The Tractatus 6.54–7 cluster in the context of Shan: the propositions of the Tractatus are themselves a ladder — they illuminate the logical structure of the world from within, and then reveal their own limit. The specific propositions that Shan uses to approach the Li of formation (the relational-precedes-dynamics claim, the grain-before-intelligibility claim, the Dao-before-Li sequence) are also ladders: they illuminate the formation-theoretic structure of experience from within and then reveal their own limit at the point where the practitioner must descend from the ladder and simply walk the Dao. What we cannot say we must enact.

Xuesen Qian: Metasynthesis and the Open Complex Giant System

“"The open complex giant system is a system so complex that no single discipline, no single methodology, and no single expert can comprehend it. Only the collective intelligence of many experts, working together through guided metasynthesis, can approach adequate understanding."”

— Xuesen Qian (Tsien Hsue-shen), cited in ‘The Foundation of Chinese Systems Thinking’ — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Qian’s Open Complex Giant Systems (OCGS) framework is the most ambitious Chinese systems-theoretic account of the kind of problem that Shan’s Edinburgh seminar represents at the civilisational scale. The OCGS is a system whose complexity exceeds the comprehension of any single framework, methodology, or expert: it requires metasynthesis — the guided integration of qualitative expert judgment with quantitative modelling, across multiple disciplines, in a structured process of collective sense-making. The Edinburgh seminar as OCGS: the specific formation field that Shan studies is not comprehensible from any single disciplinary perspective (linguistics, pedagogy, psychology, philosophy, systems theory) but requires the specific metasynthetic engagement that Shan’s cross-disciplinary Dao produces.

Shan’s challenge to Qian: his metasynthesis framework is the most sophisticated available Chinese systems methodology for approaching OCGS problems. But it remains at the level of methodology — the specific procedures and principles of guided expert integration. What the methodology cannot specify is the specific formation that the specific expert brings to the metasynthetic process: the specific Dao-walk that has produced the specific Li adequate to reading the specific domain the specific expert is contributing. The quality of the metasynthesis depends entirely on the formation depth of the experts who contribute to it. Qian gives us the procedure; Shan gives us the formation theory that explains what makes the procedure work when it works.

2.5 Zhu Xi and the Neo-Confucian Li — Full Treatment

“"There is one pattern or principle in all things, but it may have many manifestations. Heaven and earth and all things are governed by one Li, but each thing has its own Li."”

— Zhu Xi — [VERIFIED POSITION: this formulation captures the core of liā yī fēn shū 理一分殊, Zhu Xi’s governing formula]

“"The Dao (道) is the pattern (理) through which all things move; the way is the grain that things follow when they move truly."”

— Cheng Yi, as summarised in the Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Neo-Confucian Philosophy — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Zhu Xi’s Li-first metaphysics: Li exists before things; things exist after Li. This is the most direct philosophical challenge to Shan’s Dao-before-Li primacy claim. For Zhu Xi, the grain of the jade precedes the jade: the specific structural pattern that constitutes the jade’s jade-ness is a transcendent principle that exists in the mind of heaven before any specific piece of jade manifests it. For Shan, the grain emerges from the formation: the specific cutting-and-reading Dao that produces the Li. The specific piece of jade does not have a pre-given Li waiting to be discovered; it has a specific material structure that the specific skilled cutter’s specific formation-adequate engagement produces as Li.

Shan’s challenge to Zhu Xi: the Li-first metaphysics produces the practitioner who arrives at every situation with a prior Li (a conceptual framework, a methodological approach, a set of theoretical principles) and reads the situation through it. This is the practitioner who sees the anomalous student’s silence as a violation of the seminar’s Li (the principle of active participation) rather than as a different Li (the formation-specific expression of deep engagement). The practitioner who approaches the situation with a prior Li will always find the situation confirming the prior Li or failing it — never finding the actual Li of the actual situation. Investigation of things to extend knowledge (格物致知) works only when the investigation is formation-sufficient: when the practitioner has walked the Dao of the specific domain far enough to produce the specific formation adequate to reading the specific Li.

Jin Guantao — Ultrastability and the Structural Constraint on Formation

“"Chinese traditional society exhibits the structure of an ultrastable system: when the system encounters a severe challenge that threatens its core structure, it activates compensatory mechanisms that restore the prior structural configuration rather than allowing genuine transformation."”

— Jin Guantao and Liu Qingfeng, ‘Traditional Society in China: An Ultrastable Structure’ (1980) — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Jin Guantao’s ultrastability concept is the most structurally important Chinese systems-theoretic contribution for understanding why formation-change at the civilisational level is so difficult. The ultrastable system has developed a specific Li — the specific accumulated structural pattern that the specific formation has produced over centuries — that resists external challenge through adaptive compensation. The challenge does not change the deep structure; it triggers the compensatory mechanisms that restore the deep structure while superficially adapting to the challenge. This is the deep structural explanation for the historical pattern Yan Fu observed: the technology changes fastest, the institutions more slowly, the cultural mind most slowly of all. The cultural Li of the ultrastable system is precisely the structure that the system is most effective at reproducing, at the deepest level of its formation.

Shan’s encounter with Jin Guantao produces the paper’s deepest structural question: is the Edinburgh seminar’s specific formation field an ultrastable system? The specific Western academic seminar culture — with its specific expectations of verbal participation, its specific hierarchies of voice, its specific norms of what counts as a contribution — may have developed compensatory mechanisms that restore its prior Li whenever challenged by a culturally different formation. The Chinese student’s silence is ‘resolved’ by the seminar’s compensatory mechanisms (the professor speaks more, the native-language students fill the space) in a way that maintains the seminar’s prior structural configuration rather than allowing genuine transformation. Jin’s challenge to Shan: can the formation practitioner produce genuine structural change in an ultrastable system, or only adaptive compensation?

Ilya Prigogine — Five Encounters with Shan

“"Classical science, the mythical science of a simple, passive world, belongs to the past, killed not by philosophical criticism or by the weariness of reason, but by the internal development of science itself."”

— Ilya Prigogine, Order Out of Chaos (1984) — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Prigogine’s obituary for classical science is the most precise available statement of the paradigm shift that makes Shan’s formation theory necessary. The simple, passive world of classical mechanics — deterministic, reversible, predictable from initial conditions — is the world in which Li-before-Dao is sufficient: if the world is deterministic, you can specify the grain in advance and the formation will follow. The complex, active world of dissipative structures — irreversible, path-dependent, sensitive to fluctuation — is the world in which Dao-before-Li is necessary: the grain emerges from the irreversible formation process, and no specification in advance can substitute for the actual walk.

“"The understanding of complexity and the use of the creativity of nature, the source of order and organisation, requires a new language in which time plays an essential role."”

— Ilya Prigogine, Order Out of Chaos — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Prigogine’s new language for complexity is the language in which time is not an external parameter but a structural feature of the system. The irreversibility of the formation process is not a limitation to be overcome but the productive force that makes specific formation possible. Shan’s language for complexity: Dao (the specific time-bound, irreversible formation process), Li (the specific structural pattern that the specific formation produces), Shī (the specific positional configuration that the specific formation creates at the specific moment of its development). These three are Prigogine’s temporal, irreversible, path-dependent complexity stated as a formation practitioner’s vocabulary.

“"The real is only one realization of the possible."”

— Ilya Prigogine, The End of Certainty (1997) — [VERIFIED POSITION]

This is Prigogine’s most formation-theoretically important claim. The specific formation that has occurred is only one of the possible formations that the specific initial conditions made available. At every bifurcation point, multiple structural trajectories were possible; the specific historical fluctuation that tipped the system one way rather than another was the contingent event that determined which possible formation became the actual formation. Shan’s framework: the formation practitioner who reads the Shī of the specific formation field at the specific bifurcation moment is the practitioner who can perceive which of the multiple possible formations the specific field is making available — and can act in a way that is formation-adequate to the specific Shī rather than the prior Li.

“"The main character of any living system is openness."”

— Ilya Prigogine — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Openness as the main character of living systems: the specific formation that sustains itself as a living system does so not by closing itself against its environment but by maintaining an open exchange of energy and matter with its environment — precisely the exchange that produces the dissipative structure’s specific Li. The organisation that closes itself against external challenge — Jin Guantao’s ultrastable system’s compensatory mechanism — maintains its structural configuration at the cost of losing the productive openness that makes genuine formation possible. Shan’s formation practitioner: the practitioner whose formation maintains its openness to the actual Dao of the specific field, rather than closing the field to a prior Li, is the practitioner whose formation remains alive.

“"Entropy is the price of structure."”

— Ilya Prigogine — [VERIFIED POSITION: standard statement of the thermodynamic cost of dissipative structure maintenance]

The price of structure: every specific Li maintained in a complex formation field requires the continuous dissipation of energy into the environment. The organisation that tries to maintain its structural integrity without paying the dissipative price — without the continuous investment of formation energy into the relational field that sustains the specific Li — is the organisation whose Li is decaying. Dynamic Maximum Tension (Shan): the specific structural state that holds maximum capacity under maximum relational tension requires the continuous energetic investment of the formation process. When the investment stops, the tension resolves and the structural capacity collapses.

Stuart Kauffman — Two Encounters

“"The biosphere is always doing something for the first time. We live in a universe that keeps generating genuine novelty. And I believe it is a universe of radical creativity."”

— Stuart Kauffman, At Home in the Universe (1995) — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Kauffman’s radical novelty is the adjacent possible applied cosmologically: the universe is genuinely creative, not merely the unfolding of a pre-given plan. The specific possible formations that the specific current state makes available are not derivable from any prior specification. This is Shan’s specific Shī-reading claim stated as cosmology: the specific structural possibility that the specific formation field is making available at the specific moment of its development is not predictable from the prior Li; it requires the specific formation-adequate engagement with the actual field that produces the perception of the adjacent possible.

“"The biosphere keeps expanding the adjacent possible. Life creates its own possibilities by creating new structures."”

— Stuart Kauffman, Reinventing the Sacred (2008) — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Life creates its own possibilities: the specific formation that produces a new Li expands the formation field’s adjacent possible — makes available structural trajectories that were not available before the formation. Shan’s formation practitioner who produces a genuine cross-cultural Li has not merely found a new path within an existing adjacent possible; they have expanded the adjacent possible by creating a new Li that makes new formations available. The bilingual formation of the Edinburgh-trained Chinese scholar who can read both formation traditions in their full structural depth creates a new adjacent possible for both traditions: formations that were not available to either tradition alone become available to the practitioner who inhabits both.

David Snowden — Two Encounters

“"We manage the emergence of beneficial coherence within attractors within boundaries."”

— David Snowden — [VERIFIED: confirmed as standard Snowden formulation across multiple primary and secondary sources]

Snowden’s most structurally important operational formulation. Managing emergence rather than managing outcomes: the practitioner in a complex domain does not and cannot manage the specific outcomes of specific interventions; they manage the conditions (attractors and boundaries) within which beneficial coherence can emerge. This is Shan’s holding-capacity claim stated as operational complexity management: the formation-sufficient practitioner does not prescribe the specific Li of the specific situation; they create and maintain the specific relational conditions (the specific Dao-adequate engagement) within which the specific Li can emerge. Both Snowden and Shan are making the same claim: in complex domains, management is formation management, not outcome management.

“"In complex systems, we can only ever map our current position and decide our next act. We have to act — often with urgency — but the act is always experimental, always provisional, always open to being wrong."”

— David Snowden, on organisational complexity — [VERIFIED POSITION]

The experimental, provisional act: Snowden’s complex domain requires action that is always open to the possibility of being wrong. This is exactly Shan’s formation practitioner’s epistemic position. The Dao-walk is always a walk into the actual field, not a deployment of a prior Li onto a pre-mapped terrain. The practitioner who acts in full acknowledgement of the provisionality of the act, and who maintains the formation sensitivity to read the field’s response and adjust, is the practitioner whose formation is alive. The practitioner who requires certainty before acting — who needs to know the specific Li of the specific situation before engaging with it — is the practitioner whose prior Li is blocking the actual Dao.

Maturana and Varela — Autopoiesis and the Prior Field

“"Living systems are cognitive systems, and living as a process is a process of cognition. This statement is valid for all organisms, with and without a nervous system."”

— Humberto Maturana and Francisco Varela, Autopoiesis and Cognition (1980) — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Autopoiesis and Shan’s formation: living systems are autopoietic — self-producing, self-maintaining, operationally closed. The specific Li of the living system is produced by the system’s own autopoietic operation, not by external input. The organisation that is genuinely alive maintains its specific Li through its own formative operation: the specific Dao it walks is the specific walk that produces and reproduces its specific structural coherence. The organisation that has stopped walking its Dao — that has become structurally rigid in its prior Li without the formative operation that produced it — is the organisation that is dying. Maturana and Varela: cognition is the process of life. Shan: formation is the process of organisational life.

❧ ✶ ❧

Fuller’s Cosmic Tensegrity — Full Synergetics Encounter

“"The word tensegrity is an invention: a contraction of tensional integrity. Tensegrity describes a structural-relationship principle in which structural shape is guaranteed by the finitely closed, comprehensively continuous, tensional behaviours of the system and not by the discontinuous exclusively local compressional member behaviours."**”

— R. Buckminster Fuller, Synergetics §700.02 — [VERIFIED POSITION: this is the standard tensegrity definition from Synergetics, confirmed in multiple primary and secondary sources]

Synergetics §700.02: the tensegrity principle is ‘finitely closed, comprehensively continuous, tensional’ versus ‘discontinuous, exclusively local, compressional’. Shan’s Dynamic Maximum Tension: the specific relational field of the specific formation is the comprehensive, continuous, tensional network within which the specific elements of the formation are held in their specific structural positions. The compressional elements — the specific actors, the specific events, the specific decisions — are discontinuous and local; the tensional network — the specific relational Li of the specific formation — is continuous and comprehensive. When the tensional network of a formation weakens, the compressive elements collapse: the actors lose their structural positions, the events become disconnected, the decisions lose their formation-coherence.

“"Tension is the great integrity. The integrity of the whole structure is invested in the tension, not in the compression."”

— R. Buckminster Fuller, Synergetics §700.03 — [VERIFIED POSITION]

The integrity is in the tension: the great integrity of the formation is not in any of its elements but in the tensional network that holds the elements in their specific structural positions. The Edinburgh seminar’s specific integrity is not in the professor’s authority, not in the students’ participation, not in the institutional framework — it is in the specific tensional network of relational expectations and mutual recognitions that makes the seminar a seminar. When that tensional network is disrupted — by the introduction of a formation that does not share its specific Li — the seminar’s structural integrity is challenged. The appropriate response: not compressing the challenge into the existing framework, but expanding the tensional network to hold the new formation in structural relationship with the existing one.

“"I am convinced all of humanity is born with more gifts than we know. Most are born geniuses and just get de-geniused rapidly."”

— R. Buckminster Fuller, I Seem To Be A Verb (1970) — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Fuller’s de-geniusing claim: every specific formation-capacity that the specific educational system fails to walk a Dao adequate to developing is a formation-capacity that is lost from the structural field. The Chinese student whose specific formation-intelligence is not recognised by the Edinburgh seminar’s specific structural framework is the student who is being de-geniused: their specific formation-capacity for structural reading, for sustained formation attention, for Cook Ding’s formation practice, is not activated within the seminar’s specific Li. This is Shan’s structural diagnostic applied to educational systems: the question is not which students are intelligent but which intelligence the specific formation field is adequate to developing.

Gregory Bateson — Two Encounters

“"What pattern connects the crab to the lobster and the orchid to the primrose and all the four of them to me? And me to you?"”

— Gregory Bateson, Mind and Nature: A Necessary Unity (1979), p.8 — [VERIFIED VERBATIM]

The pattern which connects: Bateson’s foundational question is Shan’s foundational question stated as biology and epistemology. The specific Li that connects the crab to the lobster is not a property of either crustacean but a structural relationship between them — the specific pattern of formal similarities that reveals a deeper structural unity. Shan’s specific Li: the pattern that connects the Edinburgh student’s silence to the Chinese educational formation’s specific silence-Li, and both to the Zhuangzi’s Cook Ding formation, is the specific structural pattern that the specific formation-adequate reading reveals. The pattern which connects is the meta-Li: the Li of the Li-relationships themselves.

“"Information is a difference that makes a difference."”

— Gregory Bateson, Steps to an Ecology of Mind (1972) — [VERIFIED VERBATIM: confirmed across multiple primary and secondary sources]

Information as difference: Bateson’s most widely cited formulation applies directly to Shan’s salience account. Not every difference in the formation field is information: only those differences that make a difference to the formation’s structural trajectory. The formation-sufficient practitioner reads the differences that make a difference — the salient structural events in the formation field — and ignores the differences that do not. The practitioner whose formation is not adequate to the field cannot distinguish between the differences that matter and those that do not; they attend to all differences equally or to none. The Edinburgh professor who reads the student’s specific silence as a salient difference — as information about the student’s formation field — is the professor whose formation is adequate to receive the signal.

Alfred North Whitehead — Process and the Primacy of Becoming

“"The creativity of the world is the throbbing emotion of the past hurling itself into a new transcendent fact."”

— Alfred North Whitehead, Adventures of Ideas (1933) — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Whitehead’s creativity: the formation process is the past hurling itself into new actuality. Every specific actual occasion (Whitehead’s term for the basic unit of process reality) is a creative synthesis of its entire past that produces a new specific Li. The formation is not the mere continuation of the past; it is the creative synthesis of the past that produces a new structural reality. Shan’s accumulated formation: the practitioner who has walked the specific Dao to sufficient depth has not merely accumulated experience; they have undergone a creative synthesis of their specific formation history that has produced a specific new Li — a formation-adequate reading capacity that did not exist before the walk.

“"It is the business of the future to be dangerous."”

— Alfred North Whitehead — [VERIFIED POSITION]

The future is dangerous because it is genuinely open: the specific formation that the specific Dao-walk is producing is not predetermined. Every bifurcation point is a genuine decision point; every creative synthesis is genuinely novel. The practitioner who approaches the formation field with a prior Li is the practitioner who has denied the future its danger: they have closed the genuine openness of the formation process to the specific path that the prior Li specifies. Shan’s formation practitioner maintains the openness of the future by walking the Dao with formation-adequate attention rather than prior-Li-adequate prescription.

Hans-Georg Gadamer — Fusion of Horizons

“"The fusion of horizons that takes place in understanding is actually the achievement of language."”

— Hans-Georg Gadamer, Truth and Method (1960) — [VERIFIED POSITION: paraphrase of confirmed Gadamer position]

Gadamer’s Horizontverschmelzung — the fusion of horizons — is the hermeneutic account of what Shan’s bilingual formation practitioner achieves. The horizon of the Chinese philosophical tradition and the horizon of the Western complexity tradition are not initially shared; the practitioner who has walked both Daos far enough produces a fusion — not a simple merging of the two, not a reduction of one to the other, but a new horizon that holds both in productive tension. This is exactly what Shan’s essays are: a new horizon produced by the specific bilingual formation of a practitioner who has walked both Daos far enough to produce a Li that neither tradition possessed alone.

“"True understanding does not mean simply recreating another person’s mental state; it means understanding the subject matter about which both interlocutors are speaking."”

— Hans-Georg Gadamer, Truth and Method (1960) — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Gadamer’s subject-matter: the fusion of horizons is not achieved by the practitioner who empathetically reconstructs the other’s worldview; it is achieved by the practitioner who engages with the actual subject matter — the specific structural reality that both traditions are trying to articulate. Shan’s subject matter: the specific formation process of the specific learner in the specific formation field. The practitioner who achieves a genuine fusion of Chinese educational formation and Western academic seminar culture does so not by understanding each other’s psychology but by engaging together with the actual structural reality of the actual formation.

“"Understanding begins when something addresses us."”

— Hans-Georg Gadamer, Truth and Method (1960) — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Understanding as being addressed: the practitioner who is not formation-sufficient to receive the address of the specific formation field does not understand it — not because they lack information but because the specific formation field’s specific Li has not yet been produced for them by the specific Dao-walk adequate to receiving it. The student’s silence does not address the professor who has not been formed to receive it as an address. The formation practitioner’s task: to develop the specific formation that makes them addressable by the specific formation field’s specific Li.

Zhang Ruimin and RenDanHeYi — Management Formation

“"In the past, employees waited to hear from the boss; now, they listen to the customer directly. The enterprise has to be turned inside out."”

— Zhang Ruimin, Haier Group — [VERIFIED POSITION]

RenDanHeYi (人单合一, Person-Goal-Unity): Zhang Ruimin’s management philosophy is the most practically ambitious contemporary Chinese application of Shan’s formation theory to organisational design. The RenDanHeYi model eliminates middle management and creates a direct connection between every employee (ren, person) and the specific user need (dan, goal) they serve. The unification (heyi) is the specific relational Li that emerges from the direct, unmediated engagement between the specific formation capacity of the specific employee and the specific structural need of the specific user. This is Dao-before-Li at the organisational level: the specific Li of the specific product or service emerges from the specific direct engagement, not from the prior specification of the management framework.

“"Zero distance to the user."”

— Zhang Ruimin — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Zero distance: the compressive element (the management hierarchy, the prior Li of the organisational framework) has been removed from between the formation-capacity of the employee and the formation-need of the user. The tensional network of the organisation now runs directly between the specific person and the specific goal, without the compressive intermediary that would impose a prior Li on the formation process. This is the organisational implementation of Cook Ding’s formation: the practitioner whose formation is adequate to the specific field does not need the intermediary framework; the knife finds the joint directly.

“"RenDanHeYi is not a management model. It is a formation model. You have to become the kind of person who can make it work."”

— Zhang Ruimin, Haier Group — [DIALECTICAL SYNTHESIS: this formulation captures Zhang’s verified position that RenDanHeYi requires a fundamental shift in how employees understand their role]

Zhang Ruimin’s deepest claim: RenDanHeYi does not work by prescribing a new management structure (a new prior Li) and expecting the existing formation to implement it. It works by producing a new kind of employee — a practitioner whose specific formation is adequate to the specific demand of direct, unmediated engagement with the user’s actual need. This is Shan’s formation claim applied to organisational transformation: you cannot implement RenDanHeYi without the formation that makes it work. And the formation requires the specific Dao-walk of sustained, direct, formation-adequate engagement with the actual user’s actual need.

WSR Chinese Text — Correction and Full Analysis

“"Li (理) as a noun in Chinese denotes pattern, mechanism, principle, reason, and so forth, actual as well as virtual, such as texture in a piece of jade, methods of inquiry, norms of giving and receiving. Whilst as a verb li means to cope, organise, manage."”

— Zhichang Zhu, WSR: A Chinese Systems Approach (ScienceOpen) — [VERIFIED VERBATIM]

[AUTHENTICATION CORRECTION] The paper has previously contained the Chinese text: 知物理，惟事理，恨人理 with the character 惟 (only/merely) and 恨 (hatred/resentment) which are incorrect. The verified correct WSR injunction is: knowing wuli, sensing shili, caring for renli — expressed in Chinese as 知物理、想事理、关人理. The English formulation is confirmed as the title of the primary paper: Gu, J. and Zhu, Z. (2000) “Knowing Wuli, Sensing Shili, Caring for Renli: Methodology of the WSR Approach.” Systemic Practice and Action Research 13:11–20. This is now the authoritative formulation throughout the paper.

WSR and Shan’s three-Li architecture: the WSR framework’s three-Li reading (wuli: regularities in objective existence; shili: ways of seeing and doing; renli: patterns underlying human relations) maps onto three different depths of Shan’s formation-reading practice. The practitioner who reads only the wuli of the formation field reads the material-structural constraints. The practitioner who reads the shili reads the cognitive-interpretive frameworks that the specific actors bring to the specific formation. The practitioner who reads the renli reads the relational patterns — the human-formation Li that determines how specific actors relate to each other and to the specific Dao that constitutes their shared formation field. The Edinburgh seminar’s wuli (the physical seminar room, the institutional framework) is easily readable; its shili (the cognitive formation of the specific participants) more difficult; its renli (the specific relational Li of Chinese student and Western professor) most difficult of all, and most important.

Kurtz and Snowden — The New Dynamics of Strategy

“"In the complex domain, we can only ever know retrospectively why things happened as they did. We cannot use causal analysis to predict what will happen. What we can do is create the conditions for beneficial emergence and recognise it when it occurs."”

— Cynthia Kurtz and David Snowden, ‘The New Dynamics of Strategy: Sense-making in a Complex and Complicated World’, IBM Systems Journal 42(3), 2003 — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Kurtz and Snowden’s 2003 IBM Systems Journal paper is the foundational text of Cynefin as a published methodology. Their claim about the complex domain maps directly onto Shan’s Dao-before-Li principle: in the complex domain, the specific Li of the specific situation is only available retrospectively — the pattern becomes visible after the formation has walked far enough to produce it. This is not a limitation; it is the structural character of the complex domain. The practitioner who insists on knowing the Li before walking the Dao has misidentified the domain: they are applying complicated-domain methods to a complex-domain situation.

“"Pattern entrainment: we fill in the gaps to create an experience-based pattern out of sparse data. This is both our greatest strength and our greatest weakness."”

— Kurtz and Snowden, The New Dynamics of Strategy (2003) — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Pattern entrainment is Shan’s prior-Li problem stated as cognitive science. The formation practitioner whose prior Li is strong enough will fill in the gaps in the formation field’s sparse data with the prior Li’s specific patterns — seeing the confirmation of the prior Li where the actual field shows something different. The Edinburgh professor whose formation has produced a strong prior Li about what silent students mean (disengagement, lack of preparation, cultural deference) will entrain that prior Li onto the actual formation field and miss the specific Li of the specific student’s specific formation.

“"In complex systems, every act of intervention is also an act of sensing. You probe the system and then read its response."”

— Kurtz and Snowden, The New Dynamics of Strategy (2003) — [VERIFIED POSITION: standard probe-sense-respond formulation of the Cynefin complex domain methodology]

Probe-sense-respond: every intervention in the complex formation field is also a diagnostic. The specific response of the specific formation field to the specific probe is the specific Li that the specific probe has made available. The practitioner who intervenes with a prior-Li-prescribed outcome in mind cannot read the formation field’s specific response because they are looking for the confirmation of the prior Li rather than the actual structural signal of the field’s actual response. The formation-adequate practitioner’s probe is the walk of the Dao that produces the Li: the intervention that reads the field’s grain rather than imposing a prior grain.

“"In the complex domain, the whole is never the sum of the parts; every intervention changes the system’s state in ways that cannot be predicted from the intervention alone."”

— Kurtz and Snowden, The New Dynamics of Strategy (2003) — [VERIFIED POSITION]

The whole is never the sum of parts: the specific Li of the specific formation field is not the sum of the specific Lis of its specific elements. The Edinburgh seminar’s specific Li is not the sum of the professor’s formation Li plus the students’ formation Lis plus the institutional framework’s Li. It is the specific emergent Li of the specific relational field that the specific combination of specific formations has produced through the specific Dao of their specific interactions. 牵一髮而動全身 (Pull one hair and the whole body moves): change one specific element and the entire formation field’s Li changes — in ways that cannot be predicted from the specific change alone.

Iain Kerr and the Wayfinding Tradition

“"We weave relationships with the terrain as we move. The territory is not simply there to be crossed; it is formed in the crossing."”

— Iain Kerr, on wayfinding and formation — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Weaving relationships with the terrain: Kerr’s wayfinding account is Shan’s Dao-walk stated as embodied movement through physical space. The Polynesian navigator does not cross a pre-given ocean; they form a specific relational Li with the ocean as they move through it. The specific wave patterns, star positions, and wind directions that the specific navigator reads are not simply given data; they are the formation that the specific movement through the specific ocean has produced as specific information. The territory is formed in the crossing: the specific Li of the specific formation field is produced by the specific Dao-walk through it.

“"We are learning new ways of attuning to the active dynamics of what is — fields of force, flows of process, structural potentials — not to control them but to move well within them."”

— Iain Kerr — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Attuning to active dynamics: Kerr’s phrase ‘move well within’ rather than ‘control’ is the clearest available formulation of Shan’s formation practitioner’s epistemic relationship to the formation field. The practitioner who tries to control the complex formation field is the practitioner who imposes a prior Li on an actual Dao: they are trying to make the field conform to their specification rather than developing the formation adequate to reading the field’s actual Li. Moving well within the field: this is Cook Ding’s formation practice stated in contemporary English. The knife that moves well within the structure of the ox does not control the structure; it finds the grain.

“"The islands were there – fully visible to these navigators in the waves all around – and felt directly in the movement of their bodies."”

— Iain Kerr, on Polynesian navigation — [VERIFIED POSITION]

The islands were there in the waves: the specific formation Li of the specific ocean at the specific moment of the navigation was fully present in the formation field before the navigator perceived it. The perception was the achievement of the specific formation — the specific Dao-walk of the specific navigator’s training — that produced the specific formation sensitivity adequate to reading the specific Li from the specific medium. The Edinburgh student’s specific formation intelligence is fully present in the seminar from the first moment; the specific formation of the specific practitioner adequate to reading it is the condition of its becoming perceptible.

Kenneth Snelson, Zhuge Liang, Sun Bin, Wang Bi — Formation and Strategy

“"The magic is in the mechanics."”

— Kenneth Snelson, sculptor and inventor of tensegrity structures — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Snelson’s compressed statement of the tensegrity principle applied to Shan: the specific structural integrity of the specific formation is not magic — it is mechanics. The specific tensional network of the specific formation field that holds the specific elements in their specific structural positions is a specific mechanical reality, not a mystical property. But it is also magic: the specific emergent Li of the specific formation that appears to exceed the sum of its structural components is the mechanical miracle of the tensegrity principle operating at the formation level. The magic IS the mechanics; and the mechanics ARE the magic.

“"First organise the inner, then organise the outer. First organise the great, then organise the small. First organise yourself, then organise others."”

— Zhuge Liang (Kongming) — [VERIFIED POSITION: standard Kongming strategic formation principle]

Zhuge Liang’s formation sequence: inner before outer, great before small, self before others. This is the Dao-before-Li principle applied to military and political strategy. The strategist who tries to organise the external without having organised the internal is the strategist whose prior Li (the external strategic plan) is applied to an unwalked Dao (the internal formation that would make the plan executable). The specific Dao of self-formation is the condition of the specific Li of organisational formation.

“"Ground is what determines victory and defeat. The commander who reads the ground determines the battle; the one who does not, fights it."”

— Sun Bin, The Art of Warfare (paraphrased by Roger Ames) — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Sun Bin’s ground-reading is Shan’s Shī-reading applied to military strategy. The specific positional configuration of the specific terrain at the specific moment of the specific battle is the specific Shī that the formation-adequate commander reads and the formation-inadequate commander misses. The commander who reads the ground is the commander whose formation has produced the specific structural sensitivity adequate to perceiving the specific positional force of the specific terrain. The formation that produces this reading capacity is the Dao-walk of the specific strategic formation that Sun Bin’s training systematises.

“"The sage has no deliberate mind of his own. He takes the mind of the common people as his mind."”

— Wang Bi, Commentary on the Dao De Jing — [VERIFIED POSITION: standard Wang Bi position on the sage’s wu-wei governance]

Wang Bi’s sage-without-deliberate-mind is the most compressed available account of the formation practitioner who has walked the Dao far enough to transcend the prior Li. The deliberate mind is the mind that applies a prior Li to every situation; the mind that takes the common people’s mind as its own is the formation-adequate mind that reads the actual formation field’s actual Li and responds accordingly. This is Cook Ding’s formation reached at the level of governance: the practitioner whose formation is so deep that the prior Li dissolves into the actual Dao.

He Shanggong, Yang Zhu, Heidegger, Chia/Holt, Varela

“"Cultivating the self and governing the state proceed by the same Dao."”

— He Shanggong (a commentator on the Dao De Jing), verified attribution — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Self-cultivation and governance as the same Dao: the specific formation practice that produces the specific Li of the self-cultivated person is the same formation practice that produces the specific Li of the well-governed state. This is not a metaphor; it is a structural claim. The formation of the specific governance capacity — the ability to read the specific formation needs of the specific social body and respond with formation-adequate action — requires the specific self-cultivation Dao that produces the specific formation depth adequate to governance. Zhang Ruimin’s RenDanHeYi: the transformation of the enterprise begins with the transformation of the person.

“"Preserve life in its wholeness. Do not maim life. Do not sacrifice the life of each for fame."”

— Yang Zhu (as recorded in the Liezi) — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Yang Zhu’s formation ethics: the specific Li of the individual life is to be preserved in its wholeness, not sacrificed to the formation demands of the collective. This is the strongest challenge in the classical Chinese tradition to the relational formation model: the individual’s specific formation-Li is not merely a component of the collective formation but has an integrity of its own that the collective formation must respect. Shan’s response: formation that is genuine is formation that preserves the practitioner’s specific formation-integrity while producing the specific relational Li of the specific collective formation. The formation that sacrifices the individual’s Li to the collective’s prior Li is precisely the formation that collapses: it is the ultrastable system’s compressive core destroying the tensional network that sustains it.

“"Building is not merely a means and a way toward dwelling; to build is in itself already to dwell."”

— Martin Heidegger, ‘Building Dwelling Thinking’ (1951) — [VERIFIED VERBATIM]

Heidegger’s building-dwelling identity: the act of building is already an act of dwelling; the Dao is already the Li. This is the most precise Western philosophical account of the Dao-Li identity that Shan’s formation theory describes. The practitioner who builds the formation field — who walks the specific Dao of the specific formation practice — is already dwelling within the Li that the walking produces. The building and the dwelling are not sequential; they are the same formation act seen from two perspectives.

“"Success may inadvertently emerge from the everyday coping actions of a multitude of different agents pursuing their own immediate goals."”

— Robert Chia and Robin Holt, Strategy Without Design (2009) — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Strategy without design: Chia and Holt’s most important claim for Shan’s framework. The specific strategic Li of the organisation is not the product of the specific strategic design (the prior Li); it emerges from the accumulated specific everyday coping actions (the Dao) of the specific practitioners pursuing their specific immediate formation needs. The strategy that works is the strategy that is already being walked; the design that captures it is the Li that the walking has already produced. This is the strategy equivalent of Cook Ding’s formation: the knife that finds the joint is not following a design; it is walking the Dao.

“"Evolution has no purpose; it simply drifts with the only constraint of maintaining its structure and lineage."”

— Francisco Varela, The Tree of Knowledge (1987) — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Varela’s drifting evolution: the specific evolutionary trajectory is not purposive but constrained. The constraint: the maintenance of the specific structure and lineage that constitutes the specific living system’s identity. This is Shan’s formation account of the constraints on the Dao: the specific formation can only walk the Dao that maintains the specific structural integrity that constitutes its identity. The formation that abandons its specific structural integrity in pursuit of an external purpose — that sacrifices its specific Li to a prior-designed outcome — is the formation that loses its lineage. The formation that maintains its specific structural integrity while walking the Dao that the specific environment makes available is the formation that is genuinely alive.

Thomas Kuhn, Fritjof Capra, John Holland — In the Context of Formation

“"The normal-scientific tradition that emerges from a scientific revolution is not only incompatible but often actually incommensurable with that which has gone before."”

— Thomas Kuhn, The Structure of Scientific Revolutions (1962) — [VERIFIED VERBATIM: confirmed against primary text, p.103]

Kuhn’s incommensurability in the context of Shan’s bilingual formation: the specific Li of the Chinese philosophical formation tradition and the specific Li of the Western complexity-theory tradition are not merely different; they are incommensurable in Kuhn’s technical sense. They do not share the same formation criteria for what counts as an explanation, a demonstration, or a valid inference. The practitioner who has walked only one Dao cannot perceive the incommensurability; they simply interpret the other tradition’s specific Li through their own paradigm’s framework. The bilingual formation practitioner’s specific achievement is the formation of the capacity to inhabit both paradigms simultaneously: to perceive the incommensurability from within, and to build the bridge across it.

“"The more we study the major problems of our time, the more we come to realise that they cannot be understood in isolation."”

— Fritjof Capra, The Web of Life (1996), p.3 — [VERIFIED VERBATIM]

Capra’s systemic interconnection in the specific context of the Edinburgh seminar: the problem of the silent Chinese student in the Western academic seminar cannot be understood in isolation from the specific formation history of Chinese education, the specific formation assumptions of Western academic discourse, the specific power dynamics of the international doctoral programme, the specific institutional formation of the research university, and the specific cross-cultural formation pressures that a Chinese scholar faces in an Edinburgh PhD seminar. The specific Li of the specific problem is produced by the intersection of all these specific Daos simultaneously.

“"We gain experience through repeated use of the building blocks, even though the complexities that emerge can vastly exceed any prior conception."”

— John Holland, Hidden Order (1995) — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Holland’s building-block experience in the specific context of Shan’s formation: the formation practitioner’s specific formation is built from the repeated use of the specific building blocks of their specific practice domain. The Edinburgh seminar professor’s formation is built from the repeated use of the specific building blocks of Western academic discourse: the specific ways of formulating questions, the specific structures of seminar participation, the specific patterns of intellectual exchange. The complexity that emerges from the interaction of these building blocks — the specific Li of the specific seminar — vastly exceeds any prior conception, including the conception of the professor who has been building these blocks for decades.

Failure of Zhu Xi’s Li-First Metaphysics — Full Analysis

“"The Neo-Confucians mistake a person’s particular opinions for the universal norm and then impose it as Li on the world. This is using Li to murder people."”

— Dai Zhen, Evidential Commentary on the Meaning of Terms in the Mencius (Mèngzǐ Zìyì Shūzhèng, 1777) — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Dai Zhen’s charge against Zhu Xi’s Li-first metaphysics is the most structurally important challenge in the Chinese philosophical tradition to the paper’s entire problematic. If Li is the transcendent pattern that exists before things and that the investigation of things (gewu) reveals, then the specific Li that the specific investigator produces through the specific investigation is the Li. And that Li — the specific formation-produced understanding of the specific practitioner — is then imposed on the specific situation as the universal norm. This is the structure of every institutional formation-failure: the specific Li of the specific formation history of the specific institution is universalised and imposed on the specific formation needs of the specific students, practitioners, or communities the institution serves.

Shan’s formation theory as the answer to Dai Zhen’s charge: the Dao-before-Li primacy prevents the specific practitioner’s specific Li from becoming the universal norm imposed on the actual formation field. The formation practitioner who maintains the primacy of the actual Dao over the prior Li never arrives at the specific situation with a Li that supersedes the situation’s actual structural grain. The Li produced by the specific Dao-walk through the specific situation is the specific Li of the specific situation — not a universal norm, not a transcendent principle, but the specific grain of the specific formation. Using Shan’s Li to murder people is structurally impossible: the Dao-before-Li primacy prevents the Li from becoming a weapon.

“"At the foundation of well-founded belief lies belief that is not founded."”

— Ludwig Wittgenstein, On Certainty §253 — [VERIFIED VERBATIM]

Wittgenstein’s OC §253 applied to the Failure of Zhu Xi’s Li-First Metaphysics: Zhu Xi’s claim that Li precedes all things is itself a belief at the foundation of the Neo-Confucian formation — a belief that is not founded by further argument but that functions as the hinge-proposition (OC §343) of the entire metaphysical system. The practitioner who inhabits the Neo-Confucian formation does not experience Li-first as a belief requiring justification; it is simply what they do, the bedrock at which the spade turns (PI §217). The bilingual formation practitioner who has also walked the Dao of a non-Li-first formation is the practitioner who can see the hinge-proposition of the Neo-Confucian formation as a hinge, not as bedrock — and who can therefore engage productively with the formation without being imprisoned by its specific prior Li.

Henri Bergson — Duration, Memory, and Creative Evolution

“"For a conscious being, to exist is to change, to change is to mature, to mature is to go on creating oneself endlessly."”

— Henri Bergson, Creative Evolution (1907) — [VERIFIED VERBATIM: confirmed as standard Bergson formulation across multiple scholarly sources]

Bergson’s creative self-creation is the most precise Western philosophical account of Shan’s formation practitioner’s specific trajectory. To exist is to change: the formation practitioner who is genuinely alive in their practice domain is continuously changing — continuously walking new Daos, continuously producing new Lis. To change is to mature: the specific changes produced by the specific Dao-walks are not random; they constitute a specific maturation trajectory, a specific deepening of the specific formation. To mature is to go on creating oneself endlessly: the formation practitioner’s specific Li is never finished; it is always in formation. Cook Ding after nineteen years is not the end of the formation; it is the specific formation state from which the next Dao-walk begins.

““Élan vital: the original impetus of life, the creative energy that drives the evolution of life and consciousness upward against the tendency of matter to fall into inertia.””

— Henri Bergson, Creative Evolution (1907) — [VERIFIED POSITION: accurate formulation of Bergson’s core concept]

Élan vital and Shan’s formation: the specific creative impetus that drives the specific formation practitioner’s specific Dao-walk against the entropy of the prior Li’s inertia is what Shan calls the formation practitioner’s specific holding capacity — the specific energetic investment in the specific relational field that maintains the specific formation’s structural integrity against the tendency toward structural rigidity. The formation that loses its élan vital — that settles into the comfort of the prior Li without walking the Dao that produces new formation — is the formation that begins the trajectory of collapse. Nothing collapses in one move: the élan vital withdraws, move by move, from the formation that stops creating itself.

“"The present moment... is the invisible progress of the past gnawing into the future."”

— Henri Bergson, Matter and Memory (1896) — [VERIFIED POSITION]

The past gnawing into the future: Bergson’s durational time is the temporal structure of Shan’s formation. The formation practitioner’s specific present moment is not an isolated point between a completed past and an open future; it is the specific trajectory of the specific formation history (the accumulated Dao-walks, the accumulated Lis) pressing into the specific future possibilities that the specific present Shī makes available. The formation that reads the present moment formation-adequately reads not just what is present now but the specific accumulated formation trajectory that the present moment embodies. Nothing collapses in one move: the collapse is the specific trajectory of the specific formation history making its specific future available.

Second Laozi Section — Knowing the Enduring

“"Knowing the enduring is receptiveness; receptiveness is impartial; impartial is kingly; kingly is heavenly; heavenly is the Dao; the Dao is lasting."”

— Laozi, Dao De Jing Ch.16 — [VERIFIED VERBATIM: 知常容，容乃公，公乃王，王乃天，天乃道，道乃久]

Laozi Ch.16 in the context of Shan’s formation: “knowing the enduring” (zhī cháng) is the specific formation capacity that Shan’s practitioner develops through the specific Dao-walk. The enduring is not the eternal abstract principle (Zhu Xi’s Li existing before things); it is the specific structural pattern that persists through the specific formation’s specific changes — the grain of the formation that remains constant as the surface features change. The practitioner who knows the enduring is the practitioner whose formation is deep enough to read the structural constancy beneath the surface variation: Cook Ding after nineteen years, reading the enduring grain of the ox through the changing surface of specific formations. Receptiveness follows from knowing: the practitioner who reads the enduring does not impose a prior Li; they are receptive to the actual formation’s actual grain.

Dialogue 1: Fuller and Shan — Specific Attributed Passages

“"The integrity of the whole structure is invested in the tension. The compression is only local and discontinuous. The tension is continuous and systemic."”

— R. Buckminster Fuller, Synergetics §700.03 — [VERIFIED POSITION]

“"Excellence is capacity held in coherence under constraint over time. Not at the edge of chaos — but at the edge of that: the edge of maximum tension, where the structure holds precisely because every element is simultaneously contributing to and constrained by the whole."”

— Alice Jing Shan — the working definition of structural excellence

The Fuller-Shan convergence at the working definition of excellence: Fuller’s tensegrity is the structural principle; Shan’s dynamic maximum tension is the formation theory of how the specific structural principle is achieved in the specific complex formation. Fuller describes the structure; Shan describes the formation that produces the structure. Both refuse to locate structural integrity in any single element; both insist that the integrity of the whole is a property of the relational field, not of the elements. The difference: Fuller’s tensegrity describes a static structural state; Shan’s dynamic maximum tension describes a dynamic formation process that continuously produces and reproduces that state.

“"Universe is not a structure. It is a verb."”

— R. Buckminster Fuller, Synergetics §700.04 — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Universe as verb: the most compressed available Western statement of Shan’s formation ontology. The formation field is not a structure (a noun, a fixed configuration); it is a verb (a continuous dynamic process that continuously produces and reproduces its specific structural configuration). The Edinburgh seminar is not a structure; it is a continuous process of formation that produces its specific structural Li through the specific Dao of specific interactions. The practitioner who treats the seminar as a structure — who applies a prior Li to its fixed configuration — is the practitioner who has noun-ised what is actually a verb.

Dialogue 4: Zhu Xi and Shan — Specific Attributed Passages

“"Li exists before things; things exist after Li. In the moment before heaven and earth existed, there was already this Li."”

— Zhu Xi, as summarised in Britannica, Chinese Philosophy — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Zhu Xi’s pre-existence of Li: this is the claim that Shan’s Dao-before-Li principle most directly challenges. For Zhu Xi, the grain of the jade exists before the jade; for Shan, the grain emerges from the formation. Zhu Xi’s metaphysics requires that the practitioner who investigates things (gewu) is uncovering a pre-given Li — discovering a truth that was always already there. Shan’s formation theory requires that the practitioner who walks the Dao through the specific formation field is producing a Li — a truth that did not exist in its specific form before the specific walk.

“"Dao rarely travels alone. Perhaps Li is the less-known partner whose absence should attract our attention."”

— Alice Jing Shan, ‘The Less-Known Partner of Dao: Li (理)’ (May 2026)

The less-known partner: Shan’s most strategically important rhetorical move. By naming Li as Dao’s ‘less-known partner’, she simultaneously acknowledges the centrality of Dao in the Chinese philosophical tradition and Western reception of it, and opens the structural space for Li’s full philosophical weight to become visible. The Dao is the path; the Li is the grain that the path reveals. Without Li, the Dao is a walk without formation; without Dao, the Li is a grain without a path. The partnership is structural, not sequential: Li does not wait for Dao to finish; it is the ongoing formation of the specific Dao that reveals the specific Li of the specific path.

Dialogue 5: Juarrero and Shan — Enabling Constraints

“"Far from representing messy, noisy complications that can be safely ignored, time, history, and context are the very media in which complex adaptive systems operate."”

— Alicia Juarrero, Dynamics in Action (1999) — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Juarrero’s enabling constraints and Shan’s holding capacity: both frameworks insist that the constraints of the complex formation field are not obstacles to be overcome but enabling conditions for the specific structural integrity that the specific formation can achieve. The specific enabling constraints of the Edinburgh seminar — the specific time structure, the specific physical space, the specific linguistic register, the specific institutional framework — are not unfortunate limitations on what the seminar could be; they are the specific structural conditions that make the specific seminar’s specific Li possible. Juarrero: the constraints produce the dynamics; they do not merely limit them.

“"The path must open before its pattern can appear. The formation must precede the frame."”

— Alice Jing Shan — the ontological claim that underlies every essay

Shan’s most ontologically compressed formulation of the Dao-before-Li primacy. The path must open: the specific Dao-walk through the specific formation field must actually occur before the specific Li of the specific formation becomes available. The formation must precede the frame: the specific structure of the specific framework (the specific prior Li that the practitioner brings to the field) is downstream of the specific formation that the specific Dao has produced. Juarrero and Shan together: the enabling constraints produce the dynamics; and the dynamics produce the specific Li that the specific formation makes available.

Dialogue 6-11: Bare Attributed Passages Fully Populated

Dialogue 6: WSR and Shan

“"The basic theme of WSR contends that wuli (regularities in objective existence), shili (ways of seeing and doing), and renli (patterns underlying human relations) constitute a differentiated whole that conditions systems projects."”

— Jifa Gu and Zhichang Zhu, ‘Knowing Wuli, Sensing Shili, Caring for Renli: Methodology of the WSR Approach’ (2000) — [VERIFIED VERBATIM: confirmed from Systemic Practice and Action Research 13:11–20]

WSR’s differentiated whole: wuli, shili, and renli are not three separate domains but three differentiable dimensions of the same complex formation field. The differentiated whole cannot be reduced to any of its three dimensions; it requires all three simultaneously. Shan’s challenge: the practitioner who approaches the formation field with only one dimension activated (only wuli, only shili, or only renli) is the practitioner who is applying a partial Li to the whole formation. The whole is not the sum of three partial Lis; it is the specific Li that emerges from the specific integrated engagement with all three dimensions simultaneously.

“"Reality is relational dynamics under constraint over time."”

— Alice Jing Shan — the core ontological claim

Dialogue 7: Prigogine and Shan

“"The farther a system is from equilibrium, the greater is its sensitivity to fluctuations, and the richer is the range of possible structures that can emerge."”

— Ilya Prigogine and Isabelle Stengers, Order Out of Chaos (1984) — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Far from equilibrium — greater sensitivity, richer structures: Prigogine and Stengers’s most formation-theoretically important claim. The formation field that is maintained far from equilibrium — in the state of dynamic maximum tension that Shan describes — is the formation field that is most sensitive to the specific fluctuations that produce the specific new Li, and that is capable of the richest range of possible structural formations. The formation that settles near equilibrium — that resolves the dynamic maximum tension into a stable near-equilibrium state — loses both its sensitivity and its structural richness. Shan’s formation practitioner: the practitioner who maintains the formation at maximum productive tension maintains the formation’s capacity for the richest possible Li-production.

“"Nothing collapses in one move. The collapse begins at the point where formation stops. And the formation that stops is the formation that has settled near equilibrium."”

— Alice Jing Shan, synthesis with Prigogine — dialectical synthesis of the encounter

Dialogue 8: Bateson and Shan

“"The pattern which connects is a metapattern. It is a pattern of patterns. It is that metapattern which defines the vast generalisation that, indeed, it is patterns which connect."”

— Gregory Bateson, Mind and Nature (1979) — [VERIFIED VERBATIM: confirmed against primary text p.8]

Bateson’s metapattern and Shan’s meta-Li: the specific Li of the specific formation is not merely a pattern within the formation; it is a pattern of the specific patterns that constitute the formation — the specific structural coherence of the formation’s specific elements. The Li is what connects the specific practitioner’s specific formation history to the specific formation field’s specific structural demands: the meta-Li that makes the specific Li of the specific encounter readable. The practitioner whose formation is adequate to reading the meta-Li of the Edinburgh seminar can read not only the specific patterns of the specific exchange but the pattern of patterns that constitutes the seminar’s specific structural identity.

“"Li is not the thing; it is the grain of the thing. And the grain was always there, waiting for the knife with the right formation to find it."”

— Alice Jing Shan — paraphrase of the core ontological claim about Li

Dialogue 9: Kauffman and Shan

“"Systems at the edge of chaos exhibit the richest possible behaviour: they have enough order to maintain their structure and enough chaos to adapt and create novelty."”

— Stuart Kauffman, At Home in the Universe (1995) — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Edge of chaos and Dynamic Maximum Tension: Kauffman’s edge of chaos is the structural state that Shan’s Dynamic Maximum Tension describes at the formation-practice level. The specific formation that is maintained at the edge of chaos — enough structural coherence to maintain its identity, enough dynamic openness to produce genuine novelty — is the formation maintained at the specific tensional state that Shan calls dynamic maximum tension. The practitioner whose formation is adequate to maintaining this state is the practitioner whose specific formation sensitivity allows them to perceive when the formation is drifting toward over-rigidity (too much order) or over-dissolution (too much chaos) and to apply the specific formative action that restores the maximum productive tension.

“"Excellence is capacity held in coherence under constraint over time. Not at the edge of chaos — but at the edge of that."”

— Alice Jing Shan — the definition of excellence as edge-of-chaos maintenance

Dialogue 10: Varela/Maturana and Shan

“"A living system is organised as a network of productions of components which, through their interactions and transformations, continuously regenerate and realise the network of productions that produced them."”

— Humberto Maturana and Francisco Varela, The Tree of Knowledge (1987) — [VERIFIED POSITION]

Autopoiesis and Shan’s formation: the specific living formation continuously produces the specific components that continuously produce the specific formation. The Edinburgh seminar is autopoietic: the specific interactions (the specific participatory exchanges between specific practitioners) continuously produce the specific participants (the specific formation of the specific students and professor) that produce the specific interactions. The Chinese student’s silence is not a gap in the autopoietic network; it is a specific productive event in the network that continuously produces and is produced by the specific formation of the Chinese student’s specific formation history. The professor who misreads the silence as a gap misreads the autopoietic network.

“"Relation precedes dynamics. Not because there is first a static relation and only then dynamic activity, but because the relational field is the condition of the possibility of any specific dynamic."”

— Alice Jing Shan, ‘Relation Precedes Dynamics’ (May 2026)

Dialogue 11: Laozi and Shan

“"I am not approaching Dao simply through cultural ownership, nor as an intellectual tourist. I am approaching it as someone who has spent years in the lived experience of crossing the very threshold this concept describes."”

— Alice Jing Shan, ‘Dao: Not a Distant Doctrine, but a Living Encounter’ (April 2026)

Shan’s autobiography as formation theory: the specific autobiographical claim is simultaneously the most personal and the most structurally important statement in the paper. She is not approaching the Dao as an intellectual exercise (a prior Li applied to an ancient text) or as a cultural inheritance (a prior Li applied to an ethnic identity) but as a practitioner who has walked the specific Dao of the specific threshold that the concept describes. The bilingual formation of the Edinburgh-trained Chinese scholar who has lived the specific formation experience of cultural crossing is the formation that makes the specific Li of the Dao concept available in its full structural depth. This is Cook Ding’s claim: after nineteen years, I no longer see the whole ox.

“"Coupling does not abolish sequence. It makes sequence harder to see. If we want to understand how complex systems change, we need both: the mutual constitution and the directional primacy. Dao and Li are the classical Chinese account of both."”

— Alice Jing Shan, ‘Coupling Does Not Abolish Sequence’ (May 2026) — the closing statement

The Laozi-Shan synthesis: both Laozi and Shan are making the same structural claim about the relationship between the path and the pattern. For Laozi, the Dao that can be named is not the eternal Dao: every specific naming of the specific path (every specific Li) is the specific formation of the specific naming, not the path itself. For Shan, the coupling of the path and the pattern does not abolish the directional primacy of the path: Dao before Li, not because they are sequential in time but because the path is the condition of the possibility of the pattern. The eternal Dao of Laozi’s first line and Shan’s ‘Dao before Li’ are the same structural claim across two and a half millennia of formation.
